title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: GAGANYAAN PROGRAMME
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Department of Space PARLIAMENT QUESTION: GAGANYAAN PROGRAMME प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 4:08PM by PIB Delhi The development activities carried out for Gaganyaan mission include the following: Human Rated Launch Vehicle (HLVM3): Development and ground testing of all propulsion stages and structures completed. Orbital Module: Propulsion systems for Crew Module and Service Module developed, tested and qualified.  Engineering model for Environmental Control & Life Support Systm (ECLSS) has been realized. Deceleration system, Crew Module Up-righting System, Thermal Protection System and end to end avionics have been developed and tested. Crew Escape System (CES): 5 types of motors developed and static tested. All the CES structures are realised and qualified. Infrastructure established: Orbital Module Preparation Facility, Gaganyaan Control Centre, Gaganyaan Control facility, Crew training facility, Second Launch pad modifications have been realised. Test Missions: First Test Vehicle mission (TV-D1) for inflight validation of Crew Escape System (CES) has been successfully completed.  Integrated Air Drop Test- 01 (IADT-01) and Integrated Air Drop Test- 02 (IADT-02) with simulated Crew Module for validation of deceleration system have been completed successfully. Accomplishment of TV-D2 mission is in advanced stage. Flight Operations and Communication Network: Ground network configuration finalized. IDRSS-1 feeder stations and terrestrial links established. MoUs have been signed with other space agencies for cross supports. Crew Recovery Operations: Recovery assets finalized. Recovery Plan worked out. Parallelly, various ground qualification tests towards demonstrating new systems realized for Gaganyaan are being carried out. Gaganyatris have completed generic training at Glavkosmos, Russia. Gaganyaan mission specific training is in progress at Astronaut Training facility, Bengaluru. Activities are in progress towards accomplishment of first uncrewed mission, G1. All stages of HLVM3 viz. HS200, L110 and C32 and CES motors ready. Crew Module and Service Module systems realized. Assembly, Integration and testing of Crew Module and Service Module nearing completion Integrated simulations are being carried out. Gaganyaan missions will be launched from Second Launch Pad (SLP) of SDSC SHAR. Accordingly, to meet the integration, testing and launch requirements, various elements/ facilities/ systems were planned, configured and realized. Orbital Module Preparation Facility (OMPF) is realized to carry out the preparation of Crew Module (CM), Service Module (SM) and Crew Escape System (CES) including the CES solid motors. The integration and access requirements including the checkout requirements were considered for modifications in Second Vehicle Assembly Building (SVAB). Checkout facilities at SVAB Terminal Room (SVTR) and Launch Pad Terminal Room – Gaganyaan (LTR-G) interfaces Checkout systems for sub-assembly/ stage preparation facilities (HS200, L110-G, C25-G and EB) are augmented. Additionally, Crew Access Arm, bubble lift and zip line system are augmented at Umbilical Tower of Second Launch Pad, to meet requirements of crewed missions. Environment Control & Life Support System (ECLSS) is a “system of systems” and very critical technology for human spaceflight. It is used to maintain a habitable environment during the entire duration of the mission by maintaining temperature, humidity, pressure and carbon dioxide levels in the Crew Module. This system is being developed indigenously by ISRO. Currently, the system is undergoing development tests. Flight demonstration of reduced version of ECLSS is planned in uncrewed Gaganyaan missions. This information was given by Union Minister of State for Prime Minister’s office and Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. **** NKR/AK/NM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291083) आगंतुक पटल  : 408 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Department of Space PARLIAMENT QUESTION: GAGANYAAN PROGRAMME प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: SPACE TECHNOLOGY FOR DISASTER MANAGEMENT IN LADAKH
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Department of Space PARLIAMENT QUESTION: SPACE TECHNOLOGY FOR DISASTER MANAGEMENT IN LADAKH प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 4:08PM by PIB Delhi Government of India is using satellite and geospatial technologies to monitor glaciers, glacial lakes, snowfall, water resources and landslides in Ladakh. Details of the activities are given below: Glacier inventory: A database of more than 2,000 glaciers in Ladakh has been generated using 2020-23 satellite data. Changes in the extent of more than 1,000 glaciers for over two decades were mapped. Glacial lakes: An inventory of 3219 glacial lakes of area greater than 0.25 hectares has been generated for Ladakh as part of National Hydrology Project of Ministry of Jal Shakti. Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOF) risk modelling has been done for high-risk lakes, including Katkar and Suru in Ladakh. Snow-cover mapping: Daily satellite-derived snow-cover mapping over the Indian Himalaya, including Ladakh, has been carried out from 2019 till September 2025. Wetlands: Mapped 4,912 wetlands in Ladakh in collaboration with the University of Jammu. Waterbodies: About 41 waterbodies larger than 5.0 hectares surface area are being monitored and updated using satellite data and the information is provided under the Bhuvan Waterbody Information System since 2012. Landslides: ISRO is using satellite data to periodically update the landslide inventory in Ladakh. Satellite-based projects undertaken in Ladakh during the last five years include: Cryosphere Science and Applications Programme (CAP): an ongoing ISRO project to monitor snow and glaciers of the Himalaya-Karakoram region, including Ladakh, in collaboration with State agencies, academia and institutes. Ladakh Specific Modelling and Space Applications (LAMA): ISRO/DoS is executing a project for Ladakh UT encompassing - development of space inputs-based weather forecasting model, heavy rainfall alerts and hydrological simulations for estimating snow melt, glacial melt runoff and river discharge. Satellite Integrated Landslide Assessment and Alert System (SILAAS) project (under ISRO-DMSP): undertaken since 2023 to map landslides using satellite data in Ladakh; and for generation of village-wise landslide alerts. National Hydrology Project (2017-2025): Sponsored by the Ministry of Jal Shakti, Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, covering glacial lakes mapping, GLOF risk assessment, snow-cover monitoring, evapotranspiration and hydrological drought assessment. Geo-Ladakh: ‘Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI) Geoportal with Allied Database Development for UT-Ladakh’ project has been carried out by ISRO towards development of ‘Geo-Ladakh’ geoportal and generation of geospatial database of natural resources, energy, infrastructure and administrative boundaries along with capacity building. ISRO/DOS is engaged in advanced R&D activities to strengthen space input-based early warning system for GLOF, extreme weather events, as well as landslides; the outcome from which would be beneficial for Ladakh also. ISRO/DoS provides space-based information on floods, GLOF events and forest fires to the Ladakh UT during the response phase of major disasters. Under the Space-based Information Support for Decentralised Planning (SISDP), ISRO/DoS has mapped Land Use/Land Cover, Drainage, Settlements, Slope, and Rail & Road infrastructure at a 1:10,000 scale and hosted on the Bhuvan-Panchayat portal for developmental planning. As part of capacity building towards expanding the use of space technology for sustainable development and disaster risk reduction, ISRO/DoS has been periodically conducting training programs, wherein participants from Ladakh have also benefitted. This information was given by Union Minister of State for Prime Minister’s office and Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. **** NKR/AK/NM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291085) आगंतुक पटल  : 224 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu Department of Space PARLIAMENT QUESTION: SPACE TECHNOLOGY FOR DISASTER MANAGEMENT IN LADAKH प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: OPERATIONAL STAUTS OF NAVIC CONSTELLATION
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Department of Space PARLIAMENT QUESTION: OPERATIONAL STAUTS OF NAVIC CONSTELLATION प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 4:06PM by PIB Delhi After completion of mission life (10 years) of IRNSS-1F, presently the NavIC constellation has three satellites for providing PNT services viz., IRNSS-1B, IRNSS-1I and NVS-01. To provide basic positioning service, minimum four operational satellites are required in orbit. Hence, the NavIC constellation cannot provide standalone positioning service, however timing service is functional. Armed Forces are using multi constellation GNSS including NavIC at present to promote operational services. Since NavIC is being used in multi constellation environment for most of the use-cases, there is no vulnerability for the users. Next NavIC satellite viz., NVS-03 is ready for launch and two more satellites viz., NVS-04 & NVS-05 are in advanced stage of realization. This information was given by Union Minister of State for Prime Minister’s office and Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. **** NKR/AK/NM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291079) आगंतुक पटल  : 205 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Department of Space PARLIAMENT QUESTION: OPERATIONAL STAUTS OF NAVIC CONSTELLATION प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: YUVIKA (YOUNG SCIENTIST PROGRAMME)
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Department of Space PARLIAMENT QUESTION: YUVIKA (YOUNG SCIENTIST PROGRAMME) प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 4:06PM by PIB Delhi The YUVIKA 2026 programme was successfully conducted during May 11-22, 2026 at nine ISRO Centers, namely Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC), Satish Dhawan Space Centre SHAR (SDSC SHAR), National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), U R Rao Satellite Centre (URSC), Space Applications Centre (SAC), Indian Institute of Remote Sensing (IIRS), North Eastern Space Applications Centre (NESAC), ISRO Propulsion Complex (IPRC) and Regional Remote Sensing Centre (RRSC) West. 456 meritorious students representing 28 states and 8 union territories participated in the programme. During the YUVIKA 2026 programme, the students got exposure to space science, technology, and applications through experiential learning and various activities such as interaction with senior scientists & Gaganyaatris, lectures on space science and ISRO achievements, witnessing of live RH200 rocket launch, live interaction with India's Bharati Station team at Antarctica, Water rocket demonstration and hands-on activities like working on basic robotics through programmable robotic kit, Chandrayaan-3 DIY kit assembly, Model rocket assembly & launch and sky gazing through telescope. The 2026 edition of YUVIKA enabled participation of 456 students at 9 ISRO centers as compared to 350 students at 7 ISRO centers in previous edition. At present, there are no plans for institutional partnerships to further expand the programme. The selection in the YUVIKA programme is based on merit. However, special weightage of 15% is given for students belonging to rural and remote areas. This information was given by Union Minister of State for Prime Minister’s office and Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. **** NKR/AK/NM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291081) आगंतुक पटल  : 186 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Bengali Department of Space PARLIAMENT QUESTION: YUVIKA (YOUNG SCIENTIST PROGRAMME) प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: PRIVATE SECTOR PARTICIPATION IN THE SPACE SECTOR
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Department of Space PARLIAMENT QUESTION: PRIVATE SECTOR PARTICIPATION IN THE SPACE SECTOR प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 4:04PM by PIB Delhi The impact assessment has been carried out by the IN-SPACe, the preliminary note on the impact assessment is attached herewith at Annexure-I. In the year 2026, a total investment of $ 187 million have been reported. A total of 108 authorizations, till date, have been granted to Non-Government Entities (NGEs) by IN-SPACe for various space activities which include establishment and operation of satellite/payload, launch of space transportation systems etc. The “Norms, Guidelines and Procedures for Implementation of Indian Space Policy-2023 in respect of Authorization of Space Activities (NGP)” released by IN-SPACe envisages evaluation of the authorization applications with a view of protecting strategic, security, and national interests, among others, while permitting the Space Activities by private entities. Further, IN-SPACe is working on “Safety and Security Guidelines for space activities in India undertaken by the Indian entities”, in consultation with stakeholders. The Government of India, has undertaken various initiatives and schemes to support space startups.  The following initiatives and policies have been brought out to boost private sector: The Indian Space Policy 2023 in place where roles and responsibilities of all the stakeholders are defined Brought out the liberalized FDI policy Norms, Guidelines and Procedures for obtaining authorization from IN-SPACe are in place Brought out policy for discounted pricing policy to NGEs for ISRO facilitation Establishment of Rs. 1000 Cr VC Fund Establishment of Rs. 500 Cr Technology Adoption Fund for the development and commercialization of space technology IN-SPACe Seed Fund Scheme for incubating the idea into the product Facilitation to get access to ISRO facilities and mentorship to handhold the private   sector Skill Initiative to fill the gaps in skill requirements Establishment of a technical centre to provide testing and simulation of space systems at an affordable cost Enabling transfer of technology from ISRO Opportunity to test for space worthiness through POEM platform Providing business opportunities through various promotional events such as Space Adoption Awareness Workshop (SAAW), Industry Meets etc. In addition to the above, authorization has been granted to 17 Start-ups to carry out various space activities. In order to promote commercial utilization of space technology, the Government of India has announced the following schemes/initiatives: Introduction of a liberalized Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) policy for the space sector. Implementation of a discounted pricing policy to enable Non-Government Entities (NGEs) to access ISRO facilities. Establishment of a ₹1,000 crore Venture Capital (VC) Fund to support space startups. Launch of the ₹500 crore Technology Adoption Fund (TAF) to accelerate the development, demonstration, and commercialization of indigenous space technologies. Facilitation of access to ISRO infrastructure, technical expertise, and mentorship to support private sector growth. Launch of skill development initiatives to address the evolving workforce requirements of the space sector. Establishment of a Technical Centre to provide affordable testing, validation, and simulation facilities for space systems. Enabling transfer of ISRO-developed technologies to industry for commercialization. Providing opportunities to validate space technologies through the PSLV Orbital Experimental Module (POEM) platform. Launch of the "Satellite Bus as a Service (SBaaS)" initiative to develop indigenous satellite platform capabilities and accelerate satellite development. title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: NUCLEAR ENERGY MISSION
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Department of Atomic Energy PARLIAMENT QUESTION: NUCLEAR ENERGY MISSION प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 4:13PM by PIB Delhi Keeping in view the energy security, clean energy generation and net-zero targets of the country, the Government has announced an ambitious Nuclear Energy Mission for Viksit Bharat with a target of reaching a nuclear power capacity of 100 GW by 2047. The Government has also enacted the SHANTI Act to enable a wider participation of both public and private sectors. The aforementioned target envisages a significant contribution from indigenous PHWR technology based nuclear power plants. Further, the Government has announced measures for enabling R&D in SMRs and new advanced technologies. Towards the expansion of Fast Breeder Reactors, Government of India has approved the pre-project activities of 2 x 500 MW FBR 1 & 2 at Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu. In the last three years, no new nuclear power projects were sanctioned. However, major achievements in the nuclear power sector include; · Capacity addition of 2100 MW with commercial operation of KAPP-3&4 (2 X 700 MW) and RAPP-7 (700 MW). Laying of foundation stone by Hon’ble Prime Minister for Units-1 to 4 of the Mahi Banswara Rajasthan Atomic Power Project in Banswara, Rajasthan. The project is being implemented by subsidiary of NPCIL - ASHVINI (a JV of NPCIL & NTPC). TAPS- 1 & 2, the world's oldest operating nuclear reactors, resumed operation after successful completion of major refurbishment works. · Construction of Kaiga Units-5&6 in the state of Karnataka commenced construction with the ‘First Pour of Concrete’ (FPC) after obtaining requisite statutory and regulatory clearances. PFBR attained criticality on 06 th April, 2026. The Government has enacted the SHANTI Act to enable wider participation in nuclear power, both by public and private sector. Once the rules are framed under SHANTI Act, 2025, it is open for the states, industries and research institutions to collaborate with the Government. This information was given by Union Minister of State for Prime Minister’s office and Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. ***** NKR/AK/NM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291090) आगंतुक पटल  : 132 Department of Atomic Energy PARLIAMENT QUESTION: NUCLEAR ENERGY MISSION प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: NATIONAL NUCLEAR MEDICINE EXPANSION PROGRAMME
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Department of Atomic Energy PARLIAMENT QUESTION: NATIONAL NUCLEAR MEDICINE EXPANSION PROGRAMME प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 4:06PM by PIB Delhi Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), a Research & Development (R&D) unit of Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) is contributing in the field of nuclear medicine through its clinical patient services units at Radiation Medicine Centre (RMC), Mumbai and Radiation Medicine Research Centre (RMRC), Kolkata for diagnostic and therapeutic services for cancer treatment. At Variable Energy Cyclotron Centre (VECC), a R&D Unit of DAE, the 30 MeV medical cyclotron is operated for commercial production of radioisotopes/ radiopharmaceuticals for cancer diagnostics. The radioisotopes / radiopharmaceuticals, produced at the Medical Cyclotron Facility of VECC, are being delivered on regular basis to various hospitals/ Nuclear Medicine Centres. Tata Memorial Centre (TMC), an Aided Institute under the administrative control of the DAE has established following diagnostic and therapeutic services by utilizing nuclear techniques in the fight against cancer: Gamma Camera and its associated radiopharmacy lab: This Unit is equipped to perform multiple types of functional imaging helping with cancer staging with scans such as 99mTc PSMA (Prostate-specific Membrane Antigen) etc. other imaging services help with assessing the function such as Multigated Acquisition (MUGA) imaging to assess cardiac function etc. Positron Emission Tomography-Computed Tomography (PETCT) and its radiopharmacy lab: This Unit primarily works for cancer staging, most commonly used radioactive pharmaceutical is 18F FDG (Fluorodeoxyglucose) which is used in majority of cancers for staging such as for evaluation of carcinoma lung, carcinoma oesophagus, breast cancer, lymphoma, etc. Radioactive Pharmaceuticals such as Ga68 DOTANOC, Ga68 FAPI - Fibroblast Activation Protein Inhibitor (all prepared and quality checked in house) are utilized for evaluation of various cancers [such as prostate cancer, Neuroendocrine Tumors, Mucinous and Signet Gastro intestinal (GI) cancers etc.] High dose Radionuclide therapy ward and its radiopharmacy lab: 6 bedded high dose therapy ward has been designed as per Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) guidelines with appropriate layout and provision of a delay tank to contain radioactive sewage for proper disposal of contaminated patient sewage. Iodine-131 (I-131) is utilized for treatment of thyroid cancer, Lutetium-177 (Lu-177) PSMA and Lu-177 DOTANOC for management of prostate cancer, neuroendocrine cancer and other Somatostatin Receptor (SSTR) expressing malignancies. TMC also works on project conception, development of product for known medical and healthcare uses. After development by the laboratory, testing and solutions for errors and noncompliance are addressed till the first version is built. It is put to field use and tested and subsequent versions are developed. Example: Development of medical devices like 90Y Bhabhspheres for Trans arterial radio embolization: conceived, developed and tested and upgraded by Bhabha Atomic Research Centre/Board of Radiation & Isotope Technology (BARC/BRIT) & TMC. Development of Blood Irradiator. Development of Bhabhatron. Development of Radio protectors by BARC, and testing and Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI) approval done by TMC. Currently radioisotopes are produced through research reactors and cyclotrons. Radioisotopes  like Ruthenium-106, Caesium-137, and Strontium-90 milked into Yttrium-90 are recovered through reprocessing of High-Level Liquid Waste (HLLW). A dedicated Isotope Production Reactor (IPR) is being constructed for enhancing domestic production of medical isotopes. The reactor is proposed to be established at BARC, Visakhapatnam. Operationalisation of IPR can make India self-reliant in the field of radioisotopes. BARC also regularly produces radioisotopes and radiopharmaceuticals and supplies them through BRIT to nuclear medicine centres across India, thereby supporting timely availability for diagnostic and therapeutic applications. DAE is strengthening capacity-building in nuclear medicine through specialised training programmes. BARC conducts programmes such as Doctor of Medicine in Nuclear Medicine, Master of Science in Nuclear Medicine & Molecular Imaging Technology (NM&MIT), Master of Science in Nuclear Medicine Technology & Hospital Radio-Pharmacy (NMT&HRP), and Diploma in Radiological Physics (DipRP). title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: RADIOACTIVE WASTES
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Department of Atomic Energy PARLIAMENT QUESTION: RADIOACTIVE WASTES प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 4:04PM by PIB Delhi Typically, radioactive solid waste arising from nuclear power plants, including waste generated during the operational life and decommissioning of the plants, is within 0.15 cubic meters/year/MW. Records relating to the quantity and location of radioactive waste disposed of are regularly filed with the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB). Safe management of nuclear waste has been accorded high priority right from the inception of our nuclear energy programme. Government of India has promulgated the Atomic Energy (Safe Disposal of Radioactive Wastes) Rules, 1987 which establishes the legal requirements for safe management and disposal of radioactive waste. As per these Rules, all facilities generating radioactive waste are required to have an Authorization from AERB to discharge radioactive effluents. The authorization specifies the volume and activity of the waste that can be disposed by the facility through designated routes. The limits for radioactive effluent discharges specified by AERB are based on the internationally followed norms and safe practices. The radioactive waste handling, treatment, storage and disposal are required to be carried out as per the well laid down procedures and guidelines stipulated by AERB. As a waste management philosophy, no waste in any physical form is released / disposed to the environment unless the same is cleared, exempted or excluded from regulations. A comprehensive radioactive waste management is established for the management of radioactive waste from nuclear power plants and back-end fuel cycle. Nuclear waste in the form of gaseous, liquid and solid is generated during operation & maintenance activities of nuclear power plants. (a) Gaseous waste is treated at the source of generation. The techniques used are adsorption on activated charcoal and filtration by high efficiency particulate air filter. (b) Liquid waste streams are treated by various techniques, such as filtration, adsorption, chemical treatment, evaporation, ion exchange, reverse osmosis etc. depending upon the nature, volume & radioactivity content. (c) The radioactive solid wastes generated during operation and maintenance of nuclear power plants are segregated and volume reduced prior to its disposal. Disposal of waste is carried out in specially constructed structures such as stone lined trenches, reinforced concrete trenches, and tile holes. These disposal structures are located both above and under-ground in access-controlled areas and are designed based on multi barrier principle for ensuring effective containment of the radioactivity. The areas where the disposal structures are located are kept under constant surveillance with the help of bore-wells laid out in a planned manner by routinely monitoring the underground soil and water samples to confirm effective confinement of radioactivity present in the disposed waste. Till date the surveillance of the disposal areas at different sites has confirmed the high degree of effectiveness of the disposal system for the containment of the disposed wastes. There has been no incident of release of radioactivity from such disposed wastes. No effect of radiation from the disposed wastes on the public or the environment has been observed. High level radioactive waste generated during reprocessing of spent fuel is converted into glass through a process, called vitrification. The vitrified waste is stored for an interim period in a Solid Storage Surveillance Facility at par with international practices as per the guidelines of International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA). Technological advances based on partitioning of the waste enables separation and recovery of useful radio-isotopes such as Cesium-137 (Cs-137), Ruthenium-106 (Ru-106) and Strontium-90 (Sr-90), for health care applications. Apart from the recovery of valuable radionuclides, partitioning technology enables separation of long-lived radioisotopes including actinides prior to immobilizing in glass matrices. Partitioning technology has significantly reduced the quantity of residual waste to be stored. Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) is committed to ensure safe management of radioactive wastes, in accordance with best practices. Nuclear wastes are safely managed/disposed as per the provisions of Atomic Energy (Safe Disposal of Radioactive Wastes) Rules 1987. The regulatory frameworks for waste management in the country are aligned with international best practices and are at par with guidelines of IAEA. Further, Environmental Survey Laboratories (ESLs) are established at all atomic power plants to regularly monitor various environmental matrices and compare with baseline radiation level recorded prior to operation of nuclear facility. The effluents from the facilities are treated and monitored before discharging to ensure compliance of regulatory limits. DAE is pursuing closed fuel cycle where spent fuel from domestic source is considered as a material of resource. Most of the useful components of spent fuel are reprocessed as fuel for future reactors. High level radioactive waste generated during the reprocessing is converted into vitrified glass through a process called vitrification. With advent of partitioning technologies, segregation of long-lived radioactive constituents including actinides and extraction of useful radioisotopes from high level radioactive waste for societal application can result in significant reduction of waste-volume prior to vitrification eliminating the need of deep geological repository in near future. This information was given by Union Minister of State for Prime Minister’s office and Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. ***** NKR/AK/NM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291074) आगंतुक पटल  : 126 Department of Atomic Energy PARLIAMENT QUESTION: RADIOACTIVE WASTES प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: COAL EXCHANGE RULES
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Coal COAL EXCHANGE RULES प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 5:19PM by PIB Delhi The Coal Exchange Rules, 2026, notified under Section 18B of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 by the Ministry of Coal on 04.06.2026, establish a comprehensive regulatory framework to promote transparent and efficient trading of coal or lignite and its processed forms. The salient features of the Coal Exchange Rules, 2026 are as follows: The Coal Controller Organisation (CCO) is the Authority to register and regulate Coal Exchange(s) in accordance with the eligibility criteria, procedure for registration, fees and charges, net worth, ownership structure and governance structure prescribed inter-alia in the Coal Exchange Rules, 2026. The Authority may specify operating procedures and issue guidelines, in consultation with the Central Government. Coal Exchange has been defined as an online platform, where buyers and sellers of coal and its processed forms, transact, trade and enter into contracts on such platform. The Authority shall evaluate, grant, renew and revoke exchange registrations, as well as approve exit schemes at the time of registration. The Authority shall exercise administrative control by approving the bidding and price discovery mechanisms, contract specifications regarding scheduling and delivery of transactions, quality of delivered coal, bid types, transaction fee ceilings, bye-laws and operating procedures. The Authority shall maintain market oversight to detect and prevent market manipulation, cartelization, insider trading, and abuse of dominant position. The Authority has been given power of intervention, power to issue interim orders and power of inspection in the event of any violation or non-compliance of any provisions of the rules. The Coal Exchange shall be established and operated with the objectives of formulating coal supply contracts, facilitating transactions of such contracts, ensuring fair, transparent, neutral, efficient, robust price discovery and dissemination, securing the efficient and timely supply of coal, in accordance with the terms of the contract. The Coal Exchange shall operate an electronic trading system and utlilise network communication for its operations. The Coal Exchange would operate a Settlement Guarantee Fund (SGF) managed by an independent committee, with at least 50% invested in safe/liquid instruments fixed deposits with the Scheduled public sector banks, treasury bills and Government securities. Coal Exchanges will have a market surveillance committee and a surveillance department to carry out day-to-day monitoring and surveillance of transactions, maintain an automated audit trail for bids, execute security audit of Information Technology Systems, maintenance of a disaster recovery site and alternate trading facility to ensure business continuity in the event of an emergency. The Coal Exchange will have a grievance redressal forum. The Authority may call for information from the Coal Exchange regarding the redressal of any specific grievance. The estimated timeline for operationalisation of regulated coal exchange is 12 months from the date of receipt of an application, for registration of Coal exchange, on dedicated online application platform opened on 15.07.2026. Any entity, including captive and commercial miners, consumers including small and medium consumers in the non-regulated sector can transact, trade and enter into delivery-based contracts on the Coal Exchange(s). The price discovery of the coal traded or transacted on the Coal Exchange shall be undertaken by the Coal Exchange through a mechanism that ensures fair, neutral, competitive and efficient prices. The bidding and price discovery mechanisms shall be conducted in accordance with the procedure approved by the Authority. The final price of the traded coal shall be adjusted in accordance with the quality of the coal traded, based on the price-adjustment mechanism of the contract executed and the quality certification issued by the coal sampling agency. The market oversight mechanism and market surveillance as envisioned in the 'Coal Exchange Rules, 2026' will prevent any market manipulation/abuse to bring transparency in the Coal Exchange ecosystem. Public Sector coal companies and small and medium consumers in the non-regulated sector may also leverage this platform to enhance market participation. This information was given by Union Minister of State for Coal and Mines Shri Satish Chandra Dubey in a written reply in Lok Sabha today. *** Shuhaib T (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291193) आगंतुक पटल  : 166 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Coal COAL EXCHANGE RULES प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Assam Exports First International Consignment of Purabi Ice Cream to Bhutan
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Commerce & Industry Assam Exports First International Consignment of Purabi Ice Cream to Bhutan Chief Minister Dr Himanta Biswa Sarma Flags Off First Purabi Ice Cream Export Consignment to Bhutan प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 2:01PM by PIB Delhi Marking a significant milestone for Assam's dairy sector and the North Eastern Region's processed food exports, the first international consignment of 5,627 litres of Purabi Ice Cream was exported from Assam to Bhutan, opening new avenues for value-added dairy exports from the region. The export consignment was flagged off by  Chief Minister of Assam, Dr Himanta Biswa Sarma, in Guwahati on 28 July 2026. Exported by North East Dairy and Foods Limited (NEDFL), the shipment will supply Purabi Ice Cream to key markets across Bhutan, including Thimphu, Paro, Phuentsholing and Wangdue, strengthening the presence of dairy products from Assam and the North Eastern Region in neighbouring international markets. title: Department of Telecommunications and Government of Madhya Pradesh to Sign MoU for the Establishment of India's First Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) at Gwalior
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Communications Department of Telecommunications and Government of Madhya Pradesh to Sign MoU for the Establishment of India's First Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) at Gwalior Union Minister for Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh Dr. Mohan Yadav, and Minister of State for Communications Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani to Grace the MoU Signing Ceremony प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 7:00PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India, and the Government of Madhya Pradesh will sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on 30 July 2026 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, for the establishment of India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ), Phase-I, at Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh. The MoU signing ceremony will be graced by Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region; Dr. Mohan Yadav, Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh and Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani Minister of State for Communications & Rural Development, along with other distinguished dignitaries. The establishment of India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone at Gwalior marks a significant milestone in strengthening the country’s domestic telecommunications manufacturing ecosystem and advancing the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s Aatmanirbhar Bharat. The initiative seeks to create a world-class manufacturing ecosystem for telecom equipment and allied technologies by attracting investments, fostering innovation, encouraging indigenous design and manufacturing, and accelerating the development of next-generation telecom products and solutions. The Telecom Manufacturing Zone is expected to serve as a catalyst for the growth of telecom equipment manufacturers, technology companies, MSMEs, start-ups, and other stakeholders across the telecom value chain. It will also generate substantial employment opportunities, enhance regional industrial development, strengthen supply chain resilience, and position India as a global hub for telecom manufacturing and innovation. The signing of the MoU between the Department of Telecommunications and the Government of Madhya Pradesh will formalise the framework for cooperation towards the establishment of TMZ Phase-I in Gwalior, further reinforcing the Centre-State partnership in driving India’s telecom manufacturing and technology ambitions. The event will bring together senior officials and stakeholders from the Government of India, Government of Madhya Pradesh and the telecommunications sector. title: MSCS IN WEST BENGAL
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation MSCS IN WEST BENGAL प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 4:57PM by PIB Delhi As per the National Cooperative Database (NCD), as on 15.07.2026, there are 1840 Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) across the country. Out of these, 73 MSCS are in the State of West Bengal. The Government launched the Central Sector Project for Computerization of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) in 2022 to bring all functional PACS onto a common ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) based national software. Initially, 63,000 PACS were approved under the project with a financial outlay of ₹2,516 crore, which has since been enhanced to cover 79,630 PACS with a revised outlay of ₹2,925.39 crore. Under the project, 4,187 PACS have been sanctioned in the State of West Bengal. Financial assistance of ₹50.79 crore has been provided to the State of West Bengal. This includes ₹30.54 crore during FY 2022–23, nil in FY 2023–24 and FY 2024–25, ₹15.25 crore during FY 2025–26, and ₹5.00 crore during FY 2026–27. The Government has formulated the National Cooperation Policy, 2025 to provide a roadmap for the systematic and holistic development of the cooperative sector. The National Cooperation Policy was unveiled on 24.07.2025 by the Home & Cooperation Minister. It comprises 6 strategic pillars, 16 objectives and 83 recommendations. To ensure its effective implementation, a National Steering Committee on Cooperation Policy under the Chairmanship of the Hon’ble Minister of Cooperation and a National-level Policy Implementation and Monitoring Committee under the Chairmanship of the Secretary, Ministry of Cooperation have been constituted. This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha. ***** AK/AP (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291161) आगंतुक पटल  : 115 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Cooperation MSCS IN WEST BENGAL प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: COOPERATIVE SUGAR MILL IN TARN TARAN
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation COOPERATIVE SUGAR MILL IN TARN TARAN प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 4:48PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Cooperation carried out a study on understanding the scope of improvement of efficiency in sugar cooperatives but not specific to cooperative sugar mills in Punjab including the Shero cooperative sugar mill in Tarn Taran. National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC), a statutory organization under the administrative control of Ministry of Cooperation provides financial assistance for the revival and modernization of cooperative sugar mills either directly to the Cooperative Sugar Mills (CSMs) or through the State Government for passing on the same to CSMs, with due-diligence and subject to the viability of the project as per NCDC guidelines. Ministry of Cooperation, to alleviate the operational & financial distress of Cooperative Sugar Mills, had formulated a scheme namely “Grant-in-aid to NCDC for strengthening of Cooperative Sugar Mills (CSMs)”.  Under this scheme one time grant of Rs.1000.00 crore was provided to National Cooperative Development Corporation in two instalments of Rs.500.00 crore each in FY 2022-23 & FY 2024-25 for the purpose of borrowing additional fund from the market for providing loans of Rs.10,000 crore to Cooperative Sugar Mills for setting up of Ethanol plant / Cogeneration plant and for meeting their working capital requirement. Under the scheme, NCDC disbursed Rs.10,005 crore to 56 CSMs, in the country up to 31.03.2025. This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha. ***** AK/AP (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291140) आगंतुक पटल  : 58 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Cooperation COOPERATIVE SUGAR MILL IN TARN TARAN प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: DRIVERS UNDER BHARAT TAXI
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation DRIVERS UNDER BHARAT TAXI प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 4:46PM by PIB Delhi Bharat Taxi, a cooperative-led digital App mobility platform operated by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), a multistate cooperative society is officially launched in the cities of Delhi-NCR, Gujarat and Maharashtra. As on 19th July, 2026, the total number of driver-partners (Sarathis) onboarded nation-wide is 7.97 lakh. The platform presently has 2.55 lakh Sarathis in the Delhi-NCR region, 1.01 lakh in Gujarat and  71,095 in Maharashtra. The rollout of services of Bharat Taxi, operated by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), in other cities and States is subject to operational requirements and necessary approvals. Expansion is undertaken based on factors such as operational preparedness, availability of Sarathis, completion of statutory requirements, and coordination with the concerned State Governments, cooperative institutions, and other stakeholders. Bharat Taxi operates on a zero-commission model, under which no commission is deducted from the fare earned by a Sarathi for rides booked through the platform. A nominal ride subscription/platform usage fee is charged separately from Sarathis to meet the expenditure on technology, application maintenance and expansion of the platform. The fare payable to the Sarathi is not affected on this account. Sarathis enrolled as members of Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited are entitled to the benefits available to members of the cooperative in accordance with its bye-laws and the provisions of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002. The cooperative also facilitates access to welfare and financial support for its members. This includes access to health and personal accident insurance at concessional rates, institutional credit, including SBI Mudra loans, and vehicle financing through banks and other financial institutions. In addition, orientation and training programmes are organised from time to time to familiarise Sarathis with the use of the digital platform, customer service, road safety and passenger safety. This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha. ***** AK/AP (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291137) आगंतुक पटल  : 99 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Bengali , Telugu Ministry of Cooperation DRIVERS UNDER BHARAT TAXI प्रविष्टि तिथि:

Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation IMPLEMENTATION OF WHITE REVOLUTION 2.0 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 4:43PM by PIB Delhi The progress of the White Revolution 2.0 is reviewed regularly by the Ministry of Cooperation during the Monthly State review meetings and the quarterly National Review Conferences. Along with this, the progress of White Revolution 2.0 is reviewed in the Annual Regional Workshops conducted in coordination with Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD) and National Dairy Development Board. Under the initiative, the Ministry of Cooperation has envisaged to set up 75,000 new Dairy Cooperative Societies (DCSs) in uncovered panchayats/villages and strengthen 46,422 existing DCSs. Till now, 24,097 new DCS have been formed and 31,394 existing DCS have been strengthened. The State/UT wise progress in the establishment of new DCS and strengthening of existing societies under the initiative is enclosed as ANNEXURE-1. title: PACS DIGITAL AUTOMATION FRAMEWORK
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation PACS DIGITAL AUTOMATION FRAMEWORK प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 4:41PM by PIB Delhi The Government has approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerisation of functional Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) for bringing all functional PACS on a common ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning)-based National Software to improve operational efficiency, transparency and service delivery. The Project, initially approved for 63,000 PACS, has subsequently been expanded to cover 79,630 PACS with a total financial outlay of ₹2,925.39 crore . The Project has been implemented in a phased manner across the States/UTs. The State/UT-wise number of PACS onboarded on the ERP-based National Software is given at Annexure-‘A’. The Government on 31.05.2023 approved the World's Largest Grain Storage Plan in Cooperative Sector. The Plan entails creation of various agri infrastructure at Primary Agriculture Credit Society (PACS) level, including warehouses, custom hiring center, processing units, Fair Price Shops, etc. through convergence of various existing schemes of the Government of India (GoI), such as, Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF), Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure Scheme (AMI), Sub Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM),  Pradhan Mantri Formalization of Micro Food Processing Enterprises Scheme (PMFME), etc. Under the World’s Largest Grain Storage Plan in Cooperative Sector, 1,015 PACS across the country have been identified for construction of godowns and construction work has been completed in 313 PACS creating a total capacity of 1.80 LMT. NCEL was set up as an umbrella organization for the export of goods and services produced by cooperative societies most of whose members are small and marginal farmers. Since its inception, the NCEL has exported over 14,89,102 MT of 50 agricultural products, valued at INR 5866.10 crores to 38 countries. To ensure financial transparency across rural credit lines, the ERP-based Common National Software under PACS Computerisation Project provides standardized modules for accounting, statutory audit and Management Information System (MIS) for Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS). The software enables maintenance of digital records, generation of audit trails and standardized financial reporting, thereby enhancing transparency, accountability and efficiency in the functioning of PACS. The ERP system also facilitates statutory audit of PACS by providing digital records and audit-related information required for the audit process. ****** Annexure-‘A’ S. title: STATUS OF COOPERATIVE SOCIETIES IN INDIA
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation STATUS OF COOPERATIVE SOCIETIES IN INDIA प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 4:37PM by PIB Delhi As per the National Cooperative Database (NCD), as on 15.07.2026, there are 8,53,430 Cooperative Societies across the country. The Sector-wise and State-wise details of total number of Cooperative Societies are attached at Annexure-1 & Annexure-2 , respectively. As per the National Cooperative Database (NCD), as on 15.07.2026, out of 8.53 lakh Cooperative Societies, 6.63 lakh are functional, 1.41 lakh are non-functional and 49,177 are under liquidation. The State-wise details of total number of Cooperative societies that are functional, non-functional and under-liquidation are attached at Annexure-3 . As on 15.07.2026, out of 6.63 lakh functional cooperative societies, 3.56 lakh are profit-making and 2.50 lakh are loss-making. Financial information is not available for 56,689 societies. The State-wise total no. of functional Cooperatives Societies, along with their Profit/ loss making status, is attached at Annexure-4 . The Ministry of Cooperation has taken proactive measures to convert Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), Dairy, and Fisheries Cooperatives into Multipurpose cooperative societies. This initiative aims to enhance business diversification, strengthen financial sustainability, and prevent closures by enabling cooperatives to engage in a wider range of economic activities. The NCD is used for identification of gaps in the geographical spread of cooperatives, thereby supporting the formation of new multipurpose PACS/dairy/fisheries cooperative societies. It also enables the development of the Cooperative Ranking Framework to promote healthy competition. Additionally, the Ministry of Cooperation has set up Co-operative Rehabilitation, Reconstruction and Development Fund under section 63A of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) (Amendment) Act, 2023 for revival of sick multi-State cooperative societies and providing assistance for meeting infrastructural requirement. ****** Annexure-1 Sector-wise etails of total number of primary Cooperative Societies S. title: Corporate Mitra Scheme Awareness Webinar organized by IICA Shillong, Ministry of Corporate Affairs witnessing overwhelming participation of youth and enterprises of Mizoram
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Corporate Affairs Corporate Mitra Scheme Awareness Webinar organized by IICA Shillong, Ministry of Corporate Affairs witnessing overwhelming participation of youth and enterprises of Mizoram प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 3:49PM by PIB Delhi The Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), Shillong, under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, successfully organised a webinar on 27 July 2026, for awareness and sensitisation of the Corporate Mitra Scheme for the youth, students, MSMEs, professionals and enterprises of Mizoram. The webinar for Mizoram was conducted as part of the Scheme’s Awareness Campaign, for the Northeast Region (NER). Mizoram University, Aizawl , facilitated the program, with mass outreach and participant mobilization for the event in the state, and The Institute of Cost Accountants of India (ICMAI) supported - as the “lead co-host”; with The Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI) and The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) – supporting as the “support co-host”. title: LAUNCH OF MACHILIPATNAM, THE SEVENTH OF THE MAHE-CLASS ANTI-SUBMARINE WARFARE SHALLOW WATER CRAFT
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Defence LAUNCH OF MACHILIPATNAM, THE SEVENTH OF THE MAHE-CLASS ANTI-SUBMARINE WARFARE SHALLOW WATER CRAFT प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 5:56PM by PIB Delhi Machilipatnam (BY 529), the seventh of eight Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW SWC), being built by Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL) for the Indian Navy, was launched on 29 Jul 2026 by Mrs Goolrukh Anand in the presence of Vice Admiral Atul Anand, Additional Secretary of Department of Military Affairs. The ceremony was attended by senior officials of the Indian Navy, Cochin Shipyard Limited, and other distinguished guests. Machilipatnam carries deep historical and cultural significance as it derives its name from the historic port city of Machilipatnam , in Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh, known for its rich maritime legacy and flourishing trade along India's eastern seaboard. The ship proudly embodies the spirit and legacy of Machilipatnam while reinforcing the Indian Navy's commitment to safeguarding the nation's maritime interests. The ship is equipped for Underwater Surveillance, Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW) operations, and Low Intensity Maritime Operations (LIMO), along with Mine Warfare capability . The ship will further bolster coastal defence and enhance Maritime Domain Awareness. The launch of Machilipatnam marks another milestone in the successful execution of the ASW SWC project and reaffirms India's commitment to Aatmanirbhar Bharat in defence manufacturing. With indigenous content exceeding 80 percent, the project showcases the growing capability of the Indian shipbuilding industry and will substantially enhance the Indian Navy's operational readiness for safeguarding the nation's maritime interests in the Indian Ocean Region. *** VM/AS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291246) आगंतुक पटल  : 303 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Malayalam Ministry of Defence LAUNCH OF MACHILIPATNAM, THE SEVENTH OF THE MAHE-CLASS ANTI-SUBMARINE WARFARE SHALLOW WATER CRAFT प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Raksha Mantri virtually inaugurates Department of Military Medicine at Command Hospital (Central Command), Lucknow
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Defence Raksha Mantri virtually inaugurates Department of Military Medicine at Command Hospital (Central Command), Lucknow The department, as R&D hub & Centre of Excellence, to equip the nation against emerging threats: Shri Rajnath Singh RM calls for tech-driven preventive healthcare to enhance combat readiness प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 1:23PM by PIB Delhi Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh virtually inaugurated the Department of Military Medicine at Command Hospital (Central Command) in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh on July 29, 2026. The inauguration marks the establishment of the country’s first dedicated academic and operational department exclusively focused on military medicine. The initiative aims to enhance combat medical readiness, advancing research, developing indigenous doctrines and creating specialised expertise for future battlefields & humanitarian contingencies. Established under the aegis of the Directorate General of Medical Services (Army), it marks a significant step in strengthening the operational medical preparedness of the Armed Forces Medical Services (AFMS). In his address, Raksha Mantri emphasised that while economic and social development are essential aspects of nation-building, the fundamental basis of any nation’s sovereignty & progress lies in the strength and the morale of its military. He exuded confidence that the Department of Military Medicine would strengthen national security by ensuring advanced medical support for the troops, while reinforcing their confidence that they will receive care and support in times of need. The Department will focus on key disciplines including Military Trauma and Damage Control; Combat Psychiatry & Resilience; Environmental & Operational Medicine; Military Medical Logistics; Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear & Explosive (CBRNe) Medical Response; Emergency Medicine & Critical Care; Disaster Medicine and Humanitarian Assistance & Disaster Relief (HADR) as well as Research, Audit & Data Analytics. It will also foster innovation in technology-enabled battlefield medicine, simulation-based training, telemedicine, prolonged field care and medical decision support. The Department will be developed in a phased manner, with the initial phase focusing on establishment and commencement of academic programmes, followed by the creation of Centres of Excellence in HADR and CBRNe medicine, and eventual evolution into a nationally and internationally recognised centre for military medicine. Highlighting the growing importance of military medicine, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that, just as aerospace medicine addresses the challenges faced by pilots and astronauts in low earth orbit, military medicine studies the physical and mental stresses exerted on the human body during war and war-like situations. “Our soldiers are deployed in some of the world’s most complex regions & harshest climates, exposed to diverse challenges. This new department will develop medical protocols tailored for these operational environments,” he said. Raksha Mantri stressed that, alongside traditional weaponry, the threat of weapons of mass destruction persists in the current era. In such a situation, the department will serve as a hub for research and development, equipping the nation to deal with emerging threats arising out of the rapid technologies advancements, he said. Shri Rajnath Singh underlined that, as the world’s largest democracy and a responsible power, India is one of the largest military contributors to United Nations peacekeeping missions, and the defence forces remain at the forefront of HADR operations far beyond national borders. This Department of Military Medicine will prove invaluable in enhancing expertise in disaster response, field hospital deployment, mass casualty management, and epidemic control. This newly-established Department has been conceived as a centre of excellence in military medicine and will serve as the principal academic, research and doctrinal hub for AFMS. It will provide structured education and training in military and operational medicine, facilitate postgraduate programmes in domains such as combat medicine, combat surgery and trauma care, and promote indigenous research tailored to India's operational requirements. Raksha Mantri expressed hope that the department will act as a training ground for young doctors of the Army Medical Corps in battlefield nursing and advanced trauma life support. “The department will open up a new career pathway for young medical professionals. Students will now be able to pursue super-specialisation in military medicine. This will not only enhance intellectual capital within the military, but also elevate India’s stature in medical research on the international stage,” he added. Underscoring the critical need for ‘preventive healthcare’, Shri Rajnath Singh asserted that it should be viewed as the first line of defence, prior to actual treatment. He called for developing a system that can identify and mitigate a health risk at an early stage through disease surveillance, vaccination, sanitation, nutrition, physical fitness, occupational health, and regular health screenings. “Preventive healthcare is directly linked to combat readiness and national security. We can leverage technologies such as AI, wearable devices, predictive analytics, and advanced diagnostics to enhance real-time monitoring of soldiers’ health and the early identification of potential health risks,” he said. Raksha Mantri concluded his address by describing the new Department of Military Medicine as a symbol of a revolutionary shift in the military mindset of the nation. “Together, we must transform this department into the world’s best ‘Battlefield Medicine Research Centre’,” he said. The event was attended by Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth; Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh; Vice Chief of the Army Staff Lieutenant General Sandeep Jain; General Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Central Command Lieutenant General Anindya Sengupta; DG AFMS Surgeon Vice Admiral Arti Sarin; Adjutant General Lieutenant General VPS Kaushik; and DG Medical Services (Army) & Colonel Commandant Army Medical Corps Lieutenant General CG Muralidharan; Additional Secretary, Department of Defence Shri Manish Tripathi; Commandant, Command Hospital (Central Command), Lucknow Major General Alok Bhalla, and other senior officials. The establishment of the Department aligns with the Government’s vision of strengthening indigenous capabilities and enhancing the operational preparedness of the Defence Forces. It also complements the proposed Global Military Medicine Centre envisioned under the Raksha Strategy Vision 2026-30. The inauguration marks another significant milestone in the ongoing transformation of AFMS into a modern, technology-enabled, operationally relevant and patient-centric military healthcare system, while strengthening India's preparedness for future defence and national security challenges. *** VK/ Savvy (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290970) आगंतुक पटल  : 626 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Marathi , Gujarati , Tamil Ministry of Defence Raksha Mantri virtually inaugurates Department of Military Medicine at Command Hospital (Central Command), Lucknow The department, as R&D hub & Centre of Excellence, to equip the nation against emerging threats: Shri Rajnath Singh RM calls for tech-driven preventive healthcare to enhance combat readiness प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: NIPUN Bharat Mission and Foundational Literacy and Numeracy
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Education NIPUN Bharat Mission and Foundational Literacy and Numeracy प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 7:21PM by PIB Delhi The Department of School Education & Literacy (DoSE&L), Ministry of Education (MoE) has launched a National Mission called “National Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy (NIPUN Bharat Mission (NBM))” on 5th July, 2021 for ensuring that every child in the country necessarily attains foundational literacy and numeracy (FLN) by the end of Grade 2. This Mission aligned with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, has been set up under the aegis of the centrally sponsored scheme of Samagra Shiksha - an integrated scheme for School Education. All States/Union Territories are implementing NBM. It is the first time that the age group of 3-6 years has been included in the school continuum in the foundational stage in 5+3+3+4 structure consisting of 3 years of Balvatika and Grades 1 & 2. The state-wise enrolment for Foundational Stage in Government and Government aided schools are at Annexure I . Financial assistance is provided to States and UTs for implementation of the interventions under Samagra Shiksha including NBM as per the Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWP&B) under Samagra Shiksha prepared by the States and UTs based on their requirements and priority. These plans are then appraised and approved/estimated by Project Approval Board (PAB) in consultation with the States and UTs as per the programmatic and financial norms of the scheme. The funds are released for Samagra Shiksha as a whole, based on the fulfilment of certain conditions such as pace of expenditure, receipt of commensurate state share, audited accounts, statement on cumulative state share, statement on outstanding advances, up-to-date expenditure statement, and audited utilization certificate. The state-wise details of the funds allocated (as part of Samagra Shiksha) under NIPUN Bharat Mission during the last three years and the current year are at Annexure II . The various initiatives undertaken under the NIPUN Bharat Mission to achieve universal Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN) and improve learning outcomes include:- A 3-month play based ‘School Preparation Module and Guidelines’ for Grade I named ‘Vidya Pravesh’ was launched on 29 July 2021. The goal of Vidya Pravesh programme is to promote school preparedness in all children coming to Grade- I from diverse backgrounds (Balvatika, Anganwadi Centers (AWCs), at home, private play schools etc.), to ensure a smooth transition of children to Grade-I. It provides play based, age and developmentally appropriate learning experiences in a joyful and stimulating environment leading to holistic development to bolster a child’s pre-literacy, pre-numeracy, cognitive and social skills. This Programme is being implemented across the country. From 2022-23 till date, more than 5 crore students in 8.8 lakh schools have been benefitted. Jaadui Pitara (JP), a collection of Learning Teaching Material (LTM) for 3 to 6 years age group was launched on 20th February, 2023. It is a box having 53 LTM for the foundational stage like toys, games, puzzles, puppets, posters, flashcards, story cards, play book set for students, and handbooks for teachers. The user manual and all the activity cards, picture reading posters, story cards, and instructions of JP have been translated into 22 languages. It also consists of a Trainer’s Handbook ‘Unmukh’ which is a comprehensive guide for the trainers which has an activity bank for 3–6-year-old children. The e-JaaduiPitara (e-JP) based on JP was launched on 10th February 2024. The e-JP is a mobile based application and website with play-based pedagogy and a way to disseminate the learning of Jaadui Pitara, (a collection of Play Based Learning Teaching Material (LTM) for 3 to 8 years age group). The browser can be accessed at https://ejaaduipitara.ncert.gov.in/ . Play and activity-based textbooks for classes 1 and 2 have also been prepared and shared with States/UTs (Hindi- “Sarangi”, English-“Mridang”, “Mathematics- Joyful-Mathematics and Anandmay-Ganit” and Urdu-“Shahnai”) fulfilling NEP 2020 and NCF-FS (National Curricular Framework for Foundational Stage) recommendations. Primers have been developed in 121 local languages for FLN learning in mother tongue. These are languages spoken by at least 10,000 population. Lakshya or Targets for Foundational Literacy and Numeracy starting from the Balvatika up to Grade 2 based on the learning outcomes have been developed on the basis of national and international research. To ensure continuous professional development of teachers, the Government launched NISHTHA Online on the DIKSHA (Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing) platform in October, 2020. The programme provides multilingual training modules, including text and video content aligned with the developmental goals and learning outcomes of Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN). DIKSHA also hosts a dedicated FLN vertical with high-quality learning resources accessible across the country, including socio-economically disadvantaged districts. Currently, DIKSHA hosts content in 133 languages (126 Indian languages and 7 foreign languages), and under NISHTHA FLN and ECCE, more than 15.57 lakh users have successfully completed the online training programme. This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today. Ministry of Education NIPUN Bharat Mission and Foundational Literacy and Numeracy प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                        29 JUL 2026 7:21PM by PIB Delhi The Department of School Education & Literacy (DoSE&L), Ministry of Education (MoE) has launched a National Mission called “National Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy (NIPUN Bharat Mission (NBM))” on 5th July, 2021 for ensuring that every child in the country necessarily attains foundational literacy and numeracy (FLN) by the end of Grade 2. This Mission aligned with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, has been set up under the aegis of the centrally sponsored scheme of Samagra Shiksha - an integrated scheme for School Education. All States/Union Territories are implementing NBM. It is the first time that the age group of 3-6 years has been included in the school continuum in the foundational stage in 5+3+3+4 structure consisting of 3 years of Balvatika and Grades 1 & 2. The state-wise enrolment for Foundational Stage in Government and Government aided schools are at Annexure I . Financial assistance is provided to States and UTs for implementation of the interventions under Samagra Shiksha including NBM as per the Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWP&B) under Samagra Shiksha prepared by the States and UTs based on their requirements and priority. These plans are then appraised and approved/estimated by Project Approval Board (PAB) in consultation with the States and UTs as per the programmatic and financial norms of the scheme. The funds are released for Samagra Shiksha as a whole, based on the fulfilment of certain conditions such as pace of expenditure, receipt of commensurate state share, audited accounts, statement on cumulative state share, statement on outstanding advances, up-to-date expenditure statement, and audited utilization certificate. The state-wise details of the funds allocated (as part of Samagra Shiksha) under NIPUN Bharat Mission during the last three years and the current year are at Annexure II . The various initiatives undertaken under the NIPUN Bharat Mission to achieve universal Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN) and improve learning outcomes include:- A 3-month play based ‘School Preparation Module and Guidelines’ for Grade I named ‘Vidya Pravesh’ was launched on 29 July 2021. The goal of Vidya Pravesh programme is to promote school preparedness in all children coming to Grade- I from diverse backgrounds (Balvatika, Anganwadi Centers (AWCs), at home, private play schools etc.), to ensure a smooth transition of children to Grade-I. It provides play based, age and developmentally appropriate learning experiences in a joyful and stimulating environment leading to holistic development to bolster a child’s pre-literacy, pre-numeracy, cognitive and social skills. This Programme is being implemented across the country. From 2022-23 till date, more than 5 crore students in 8.8 lakh schools have been benefitted. Jaadui Pitara (JP), a collection of Learning Teaching Material (LTM) for 3 to 6 years age group was launched on 20th February, 2023. It is a box having 53 LTM for the foundational stage like toys, games, puzzles, puppets, posters, flashcards, story cards, play book set for students, and handbooks for teachers. The user manual and all the activity cards, picture reading posters, story cards, and instructions of JP have been translated into 22 languages. It also consists of a Trainer’s Handbook ‘Unmukh’ which is a comprehensive guide for the trainers which has an activity bank for 3–6-year-old children. The e-JaaduiPitara (e-JP) based on JP was launched on 10th February 2024. The e-JP is a mobile based application and website with play-based pedagogy and a way to disseminate the learning of Jaadui Pitara, (a collection of Play Based Learning Teaching Material (LTM) for 3 to 8 years age group). The browser can be accessed at https://ejaaduipitara.ncert.gov.in/ . Play and activity-based textbooks for classes 1 and 2 have also been prepared and shared with States/UTs (Hindi- “Sarangi”, English-“Mridang”, “Mathematics- Joyful-Mathematics and Anandmay-Ganit” and Urdu-“Shahnai”) fulfilling NEP 2020 and NCF-FS (National Curricular Framework for Foundational Stage) recommendations. Primers have been developed in 121 local languages for FLN learning in mother tongue. These are languages spoken by at least 10,000 population. Lakshya or Targets for Foundational Literacy and Numeracy starting from the Balvatika up to Grade 2 based on the learning outcomes have been developed on the basis of national and international research. To ensure continuous professional development of teachers, the Government launched NISHTHA Online on the DIKSHA (Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing) platform in October, 2020. The programme provides multilingual training modules, including text and video content aligned with the developmental goals and learning outcomes of Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN). DIKSHA also hosts a dedicated FLN vertical with high-quality learning resources accessible across the country, including socio-economically disadvantaged districts. Currently, DIKSHA hosts content in 133 languages (126 Indian languages and 7 foreign languages), and under NISHTHA FLN and ECCE, more than 15.57 lakh users have successfully completed the online training programme. This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today. title: Implementation of PM SHRI scheme
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Education Implementation of PM SHRI scheme प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 7:09PM by PIB Delhi The National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 emphasises the importance of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and its role in school education. Under Para 4.24, the Policy envisages concerted curricular and pedagogical initiatives, including the introduction of contemporary subjects such as Artificial Intelligence at relevant stages to develop essential skills among students at all levels. In alignment with the vision of NEP 2020, which emphasises the integration of emerging technologies in education, including Artificial Intelligence, the Ministry of Education has undertaken several initiatives to equip teachers, school heads and teacher educators with the necessary competencies for AI-assisted pedagogy. Strengthening of teacher education and continuous professional development is supported under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha, aligned with NEP 2020. The Scheme provides support for strengthening the physical infrastructure of Teacher Education Institutions (TEIs), including State Councils of Educational Research and Training (SCERTs) and District Institutes of Education and Training (DIETs); strengthening the academic and professional capacities of teacher educators; providing continuous academic support through Block Resource Centres (BRCs) and Cluster Resource Centres (CRCs); and supporting inservice training of teachers, school heads, teacher educators, resource persons, master trainers and newly recruited teachers through the approved Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWP&B) of the respective States/UTs. Further, the Ministry implements Information and Communication Technology (ICT) and digital initiatives under Samagra Shiksha to strengthen digital learning in Government schools by supporting digital infrastructure, digital boards, virtual classrooms, training resources and other emerging technologies. The Department also implements NISHTHA (National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement), a flagship teacher capacity-building programme under Samagra Shiksha. The programme includes dedicated modules on AI in Education, digital pedagogy and educational technology. Subject-specific Level-II Educational Technology modules include digital tools for Mathematics, Science, Languages and Social Sciences. NISHTHA is delivered through the DIKSHA platform, enabling teachers to access self-paced digital learning resources. Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing (DIKSHA), the Nation's digital platform for school education, provides quality digital content, QR-coded Energised Textbooks (ETBs), teacher training resources and digital learning materials for States/UTs. DIKSHA has evolved into a robust Learning Management System (LMS) supporting end-to-end digital learning through course creation, content delivery, learner engagement, assessments, progress tracking and certification. The platform incorporates personalised and AI-enabled learning support and currently hosts more than 350 live courses, including about 59 courses on Artificial Intelligence and Digital Learning, thereby supporting continuous professional development of teachers and promoting AI-enabled teaching-learning practices. To ensure that educators remain abreast of emerging technologies, the Ministry of Education and NCERT organise regular capacity-building programmes, consultation workshops and webinars covering Artificial Intelligence, Content-Pedagogy-Technology integration, Information and Communication Technology (ICT), Open Educational Resources and AI-enabled teaching-learning practices. Recognising the critical role of teachers in leveraging technology to improve learning outcomes, NCERT has been continuously organising AI-related training programmes, benefiting more than 96,000 participants. Further, NCERT regularly conducts AI Awareness, Ethical Usage and AI Tools training programmes. CBSE and NCERT also offer self-paced online courses on Artificial Intelligence. AI capacity building programmes for teachers are also organised by Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS) and Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS) through reputed institutions. Further, under the National Mission for Mentoring (NMM), envisaged under Para 15.11 of NEP 2020, AI in Education has been identified as a dedicated sub-domain under the Digital Literacy domain to enable teachers to receive focused mentoring on the pedagogical and ethical use of Artificial Intelligence in classrooms. The National Programme on Artificial Intelligence (NPAI) Skilling Framework recognises Artificial Intelligence as a compute-intensive domain requiring robust digital infrastructure, access to high-performance computing resources and a conducive ecosystem for research and innovation. In this context, the IndiaAI Mission aims to facilitate access to quality datasets for AI research and innovation, develop a skilled AI talent pool, make AI compute and critical infrastructure widely accessible, promote core and applied AI research across sectors, support scaling of AI-based solutions, and establish governance mechanisms for the responsible, ethical and trustworthy development and deployment of Artificial Intelligence. This information was given by the Minister of State for Education Shri Jayant Chaudhary, in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today. ***** RRTN (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291332) आगंतुक पटल  : 124 Ministry of Education Implementation of PM SHRI scheme प्रविष्टि तिथि:
