title: IndiaAI Mission Advances AI-Driven Governance and Public Service Delivery through Collaborative Roadmaps, Innovation Challenges and Capacity Building
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Electronics & IT IndiaAI Mission Advances AI-Driven Governance and Public Service Delivery through Collaborative Roadmaps, Innovation Challenges and Capacity Building IndiaAI Mission Identifies 762 AI Use Cases Across 62 Ministries, Approves 58 AI Centres of Excellence and 543 Data & AI Labs प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 3:55PM by PIB Delhi India’s AI policy is based on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of democratizing technology. It is aimed at creating economic opportunities and employment for youth, while addressing risks associated with it. India’s AI strategy builds on India’s vibrant IT sector with annual revenue of 300 billion dollars and 60 Lakh strong workforce. IndiaAI Mission supports India’s AI ambitions under seven pillars, as under: IndiaAI Compute Pillar: To establish a high-end, scalable AI computing ecosystem to address the growing requirements of India's rapidly expanding AI startup and research communities. Foundation Models: To focus on the development of indigenous Large Language Models (LLMs), Multimodal Models, and domain-specific Small Language Models, ensuring sovereign AI capabilities and addressing India-specific use cases. IndiaAI Application Development Initiative (IADI): To support the development, scaling, and deployment of impactful AI solutions capable of driving large-scale socio-economic transformation across critical sectors. IndiaAI FutureSkills : To build a robust AI talent pipeline by establishing specialised Data and AI Labs in Tier 2 and 3 cities, providing student fellowships, and developing industry-aligned curricula to democratise AI education. AIKosh (IndiaAI Datasets Platform): To create a unified platform providing seamless access to high-quality datasets, models, and tools, integrating resources from government and non-government entities to foster open innovation. Safe & Trusted AI: To enable responsible AI development through indigenous governance frameworks and evaluation tools tailored to India's unique socio-economic and cultural landscape. IndiaAI Startup Financing: To provide risk capital and support throughout the startup lifecycle, bridging funding gaps from the initial prototyping stage through to commercialization. Under the Application Development Initiative (IADI), IndiaAI conducted a workshop on AI in public service delivery on 5 th April 2024, bringing together representatives from the Central and State Governments. The workshop supported Ministries and Departments in assessing their data capabilities and identifying AI use cases, fostering a consultative and collaborative approach to developing AI roadmaps for governance and public service delivery. Through innovation challenges, grant programmes and hackathons, IADI has built a pipeline of AI solutions across priority sectors including healthcare, agriculture, governance, climate, cybersecurity and financial regulation, with pathways from ideation to pilot deployment and scale. Under this pillar, the IndiaAI Mission has launched 11 national-level hackathons and innovation challenges across these sectors. The IndiaAI Innovation Challenge focused on AI solutions in healthcare, agriculture, governance, learning disabilities and climate change. 30 solutions were shortlisted in Stage 1 for pilot implementation with Central Ministries, States and Public Sector Organisations. Subsequently, five teams (one per sector) were selected for national-level deployment, with pilots underway across multiple States. The IndiaAI I4C CyberGuard AI Hackathon , conducted in collaboration with the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), developed AI solutions for classification of cybercrime complaints and identification of emerging crime patterns on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP). The shortlisted solution has been integrated with I4C systems. The IndiaAI–GSI Mineral Targeting with AI Hackathon , organised in partnership with the Geological Survey of India, focused on leveraging AI/ML for advanced mineral prognostication using geoscientific datasets such as geology, geophysics, geochemistry, and remote sensing. The Cancer AI & Technology Challenge (CATCH) , in collaboration with the National Cancer Grid, aims to strengthen cancer screening, diagnostics, treatment support, and healthcare operations. The top shortlisted teams are undergoing ethical review prior to implementation. The IndiaAI Face Authentication Challenge aims to enhance the integrity of public examinations through AI-enabled de-duplication and one-to-many photo verification. Two teams have been selected for deployment at the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), and deployment has commenced. The IndiaAI Intelligent Document Processing (IDP) Challenge aims to automate extraction, classification, validation, and structuring of information from complex multilingual documents. Two shortlisted teams are being deployed at UPSC, and implementation is underway. The IndiaAI Innovation Challenge 2026 , supported by the Ministry of Ayush and the Ministry of MSME, promotes AI solutions for AYUSH healthcare and MSMEs. Applications have been received across multiple problem statements, with Stage 1 evaluations underway, followed by prototype development and deployment. viii. The IndiaAI Challenge for Transforming Governance , in partnership with the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS), Government of Andhra Pradesh, addresses AI use cases across key departments. Applications have been received, Stage 1 evaluations are underway, and prototype development and pilot implementation are planned. The IndiaAI Financial Compliance Reporting Challenge , in collaboration with the National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA), promotes AI-enabled compliance monitoring and risk assessment. The CDSCO–IndiaAI Health Innovation Acceleration Hackathon , organised with the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), focuses on AI-driven automation of regulatory workflows, including document summarisation, anonymisation, and inspection reporting. Prototype development and deployment are planned. The PMJAY Auto Adjudication Hackathon , in collaboration with the National Health Authority (NHA), supports the development of AI-based adjudication frameworks for PMJAY claims, resulting in multiple prototypes and pilot deployments. These initiatives collectively demonstrate that State Governments are actively consulted and engaged through workshops, consultations, and collaborative challenge mechanisms in the formulation and implementation of AI roadmaps for governance and public service delivery. AI Centres of Excellence: Government has approved a scheme for the establishment of 58 Artificial Intelligence Centres of Excellence (AI-CoEs) across States and Union Territories, in collaboration with the respective State/UT Governments and industry partners.  Under the approved framework, Two Artificial Intelligence Centres of Excellence (AI-CoEs) have been allocated for establishment in the state of Tamil Nadu. IndiaAI Data & AI Labs (ITIs/Polytechnics): Under the IndiaAI FutureSkills pillar, 543 Data & AI Labs across ITIs and Polytechnics in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities have been approved for establishment to provide training in AI, data annotation, data curation and applied data science. As part of this initiative, 18 Data & AI Labs have been allocated for establishment in Tamil Nadu. IndiaAI Fellowships: Under the IndiaAI FutureSkills pillar, fellowships are provided to undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral students for AI education and research. A total of 686 fellowships have been awarded nationally across 178 institutions. Of these, 162 fellowships have been awarded to students from Tamil Nadu, comprising 96 undergraduate, 34 postgraduate and 32 PhD fellowships. IndiaAI Impact Summit: India hosted the India-AI Impact Summit 2026 in New Delhi from 16 th to 21 st February 2026. The Hon'ble Prime Minister called upon Ministries and Departments at the inauguration of the India AI Impact Summit 2026 to actively engage with the India AI Impact Expo and identify AI applications relevant to their respective domains to accelerate AI adoption across the Government. Pursuant to these directions and the deliberations held during the Summit, the Cabinet Secretariat coordinated with Ministries and Departments to identify opportunities for leveraging AI to address governance, service delivery, operational efficiency, and sector-specific challenges. This exercise resulted in the identification of 762 problem statements from 62 Ministries and Departments, which were subsequently shared with MeitY for facilitating AI-enabled interventions. The Government has undertaken the following steps to ensure that deployment of AI in Government systems, including for citizen-facing services, adheres to standards of transparency, accountability, data privacy, algorithmic fairness and independent audit: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDP Act) provides a comprehensive framework for processing of personal data, including purpose limitation, data minimisation, informed consent, and rights of access, correction and erasure for data principals; it also requires Significant Data Fiduciaries to appoint a data auditor and undertake periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments. Under the Safe & Trusted AI pillar of the IndiaAI Mission, 13 Responsible AI projects have been selected across themes including AI bias mitigation, algorithm auditing, explainable AI, privacy-preserving AI and deepfake detection, being implemented by academic institutions, start-ups, industry and civil-society organisations to develop indigenous tools and frameworks including tools for assessing model fairness and an open-source framework for participatory algorithmic auditing. India AI Governance Guidelines were released on 5th November, 2025, providing a comprehensive national framework for the safe, responsible and inclusive development and deployment of Artificial Intelligence in the country. Pursuant to the Guidelines, the following institutional mechanisms have been initiated, AI Governance and Economic Group (AIGEG), a high-level inter-ministerial body to steer the development of India’s national AI governance strategy; Technology and Policy Expert Committee (TPEC), to support technical and policy recommendations; and AI Safety Institute (AISI), to undertake safety research, develop standards, test AI systems and evaluate emerging risks. The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued advisories on safety measures against adversarial AI threats in May 2023, launched the Certified Security Professional in Artificial Intelligence (CSPAI) programme with SISA in September 2024, and issued advisories on best practices for the responsible use of Generative AI in March 2025. An IndiaAI Safety Institute is being established as a hub for indigenous research and development on AI safety, to support India’s technical and institutional infrastructure for AI governance. This information was submitted by Union Minister of State for Electronics and Information Technology Shri Jitin Prasada in Lok Sabha on 29.07.2026. **** Vinod Kumar / Kanishk Sharma (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291062) आगंतुक पटल  : 191 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Electronics & IT IndiaAI Mission Advances AI-Driven Governance and Public Service Delivery through Collaborative Roadmaps, Innovation Challenges and Capacity Building IndiaAI Mission Identifies 762 AI Use Cases Across 62 Ministries, Approves 58 AI Centres of Excellence and 543 Data & AI Labs प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: India Strengthens Global Digital Cooperation through Digital Public Infrastructure Partnerships with 24 Countries
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Electronics & IT India Strengthens Global Digital Cooperation through Digital Public Infrastructure Partnerships with 24 Countries प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 3:48PM by PIB Delhi Over the past decade, the Government of India has built a robust ecosystem of open, interoperable and inclusive digital platforms that have transformed public service delivery, promoted financial inclusion, fostered innovation and created new opportunities for citizens and businesses. The government's vision now extends beyond domestic digital transformation towards building a globally connected, trusted and inclusive digital ecosystem. Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) was one of the key priority areas of the Digital Economy Working Group (DEWG) meetings during India's G20 Presidency in 2023. The G20 New Delhi Leaders’ Declaration explicitly recognised DPI, as a development accelerator for economic growth. In furtherance of this vision, the Government of India has signed MoUs with 24 countries for cooperation in sharing successful population-scale digital solutions to accelerate digital transformation globally. These MoUs provide a framework for cooperation in capacity building, knowledge and best-practice exchange, joint workshops and expert consultations, feasibility and e-readiness assessments, and the development, piloting and scaling of proven digital solutions. The country-wise list of signed MoUs is provided at Annexure-I. The Government of India has undertaken virtual consultations and technical workshops with partner countries to showcase India Stack and other population-scale digital solutions and identify areas of interest. Based on the solutions identified, detailed technical discussions have held with the concerned Indian technical agencies and partner countries including feasibility studies to assess the readiness of the partner country’s digital ecosystem. Significant progress has been achieved with countries of the Global South, including the conclusion of Implementation Framework Agreement (IFA) and a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) with Kenya for implementation of DigiLocker.  Development of a foundational DigiLocker solution in Cuba has also commenced. Further, under the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) programme of MEA, a course on DPI was conducted for Cuban delegation in December 2025. Additionally, bilateral consultations have progressed with partner countries such as Lao PDR, Seychelles, Venezuela, Armenia, Fiji, Guyana Colombia for the potential adoption of key Indian digital solutions, including e-Sanjeevani, e-Office, e-Hospital etc. Moreover, Unified Payments Interface (UPI) is linked with the payment systems of various countries to facilitate Person-to-Person (P2P) remittances and Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions. The details of countries using UPI along with Partner institutions are provided at Annexure-II. The Government regularly facilitates study visits and technical interactions for foreign delegations, enabling them to engage with key institutions like Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), National e-Governance Division (NeGD), National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), National Informatics Centre (NIC), Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), etc. These engagements enable partner countries to discuss implementation challenges and draw on India’s experience in developing its Digital Public Infrastructure. Some of the recent study visits include delegations from Kenya, Rwanda, Nepal, Indonesia, and South Africa. The Government has also approved the Social Impact Fund (SIF), which is a government led, multistakeholder initiative to provide financial support and technical assistance for DPI pilot implementation in the Global South particularly in Low- and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs). **** Annexure-I List of partner countries of signed India Stack MoUs S.No. Recipient Country Date of Signing 1 Ministry of                         29 JUL 2026 3:48PM by PIB Delhi Over the past decade, the Government of India has built a robust ecosystem of open, interoperable and inclusive digital platforms that have transformed public service delivery, promoted financial inclusion, fostered innovation and created new opportunities for citizens and businesses. The government's vision now extends beyond domestic digital transformation towards building a globally connected, trusted and inclusive digital ecosystem. Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) was one of the key priority areas of the Digital Economy Working Group (DEWG) meetings during India's G20 Presidency in 2023. The G20 New Delhi Leaders’ Declaration explicitly recognised DPI, as a development accelerator for economic growth. In furtherance of this vision, the Government of India has signed MoUs with 24 countries for cooperation in sharing successful population-scale digital solutions to accelerate digital transformation globally. These MoUs provide a framework for cooperation in capacity building, knowledge and best-practice exchange, joint workshops and expert consultations, feasibility and e-readiness assessments, and the development, piloting and scaling of proven digital solutions. The country-wise list of signed MoUs is provided at Annexure-I. The Government of India has undertaken virtual consultations and technical workshops with partner countries to showcase India Stack and other population-scale digital solutions and identify areas of interest. Based on the solutions identified, detailed technical discussions have held with the concerned Indian technical agencies and partner countries including feasibility studies to assess the readiness of the partner country’s digital ecosystem. Significant progress has been achieved with countries of the Global South, including the conclusion of Implementation Framework Agreement (IFA) and a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) with Kenya for implementation of DigiLocker.  Development of a foundational DigiLocker solution in Cuba has also commenced. Further, under the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) programme of MEA, a course on DPI was conducted for Cuban delegation in December 2025. Additionally, bilateral consultations have progressed with partner countries such as Lao PDR, Seychelles, Venezuela, Armenia, Fiji, Guyana Colombia for the potential adoption of key Indian digital solutions, including e-Sanjeevani, e-Office, e-Hospital etc. Moreover, Unified Payments Interface (UPI) is linked with the payment systems of various countries to facilitate Person-to-Person (P2P) remittances and Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions. The details of countries using UPI along with Partner institutions are provided at Annexure-II. The Government regularly facilitates study visits and technical interactions for foreign delegations, enabling them to engage with key institutions like Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), National e-Governance Division (NeGD), National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), National Informatics Centre (NIC), Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), etc. These engagements enable partner countries to discuss implementation challenges and draw on India’s experience in developing its Digital Public Infrastructure. Some of the recent study visits include delegations from Kenya, Rwanda, Nepal, Indonesia, and South Africa. The Government has also approved the Social Impact Fund (SIF), which is a government led, multistakeholder initiative to provide financial support and technical assistance for DPI pilot implementation title: Electronics Development Fund Strengthens India's Innovation Ecosystem by Supporting Technology Startups in Electronics System Design, Manufacturing & IT
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Electronics & IT Electronics Development Fund Strengthens India's Innovation Ecosystem by Supporting Technology Startups in Electronics System Design, Manufacturing & IT Electronics Development Fund Invests Around ₹258 Crore in Eight Daughter Funds, Mobilising Over ₹1,335 Crore Investments Across 128 Startups and Companies प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 3:17PM by PIB Delhi India’s electronics sector has witnessed a remarkable transformation in recent years, driven by a series of Government initiatives and industry reforms. The country is steadily emerging as a global hub for electronics system design and manufacturing. The Electronics Development Fund (EDF) was one of the initiatives of the Government of India, to promote market driven innovation in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM). The EDF was set up as a Fund of Funds, designed to invest in professionally managed Daughter Funds which are SEBI registered venture funds. These Daughter Funds provided risk capital to startups and companies developing new technologies in the area of ESDM and Information Technology (IT).  By doing so, the EDF played a crucial role in building a self-sustaining electronics ecosystem that encourages innovation, product design, and intellectual property creation within the country. The selection of startups for investments by the Daughter Funds of EDF were made on the basis of various parameters which included their innovation capability, indigenous technology development, and IP creation potential, technical capability of the founding team as well as a scalable and commercially viable business model. Canbank Venture Capital Funds Ltd. (CVCFL) is the Fund Manager and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology is the anchor investor of EDF. As on 30.06.2026, EDF has invested Rs. 257.77 crore in eight Daughter Funds, which in turn have made investments of Rs. 1335.77 crore in 128 Companies/Startups.  The details of investments of the Daughter Funds of EDF, sector wise, and location wise are as follows: S. title: NeGP Strengthens Last-Mile Governance through Common Service Centres and District e-Governance Societies, Delivering Transparent, Efficient and Citizen-Centric Digital Services Across the Country
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Electronics & IT NeGP Strengthens Last-Mile Governance through Common Service Centres and District e-Governance Societies, Delivering Transparent, Efficient and Citizen-Centric Digital Services Across the Country Common Service Centres Increase from 83,950 to 5,01,731, Cover over 2.5 Lakh Gram Panchayats and Deliver over 48 Crore Transactions in 2025-26 Digital India Builds on the Foundation of NeGP to Expand Digital Public Infrastructure and Strengthen Citizen-Centric Governance प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 2:42PM by PIB Delhi National e-Governance Plan (NeGP): The National e-Governance Plan (NeGP) was approved by the Government in May 2006 with the vision of making all Government services accessible to the common man in his locality, through common service delivery outlets, and to ensure efficiency, transparency and reliability of such services at affordable costs. The foundational digital infrastructure created under NeGP includes: State Data Centres (SDCs), Statewide Area Networks (SWANs), State Service Delivery Gateways (SSDGs) and Common Services Centres (CSCs). NeGP also resulted in Mission Mode projects such as Passport, Land Record Management, e-Office, Computerisation of Public Distribution System, etc. Digital India Programme: The Government launched the Digital India Programme in July 2015, under which the National e-Governance Plan (NeGP) was subsumed. At its core, the programme promotes three interconnected goals: strengthening digital infrastructure, delivering government services digitally, and empowering citizens through digital literacy and employment. During the recent AI Impact Summit, President Macron of France stated that India has built a foundational DPI which no other country in the world has built. Key Digital Public Infrastructure initiatives: India has developed a unique digital public infrastructure which has enabled large scale digital solutions for our people. Aadhaar: Over 1.44+ billion Aadhaar numbers have been generated. Through Aadhaar-linked Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT), cash benefits from various welfare schemes (318 Schemes of 56 Ministries) are directly transferred into beneficiaries' bank accounts. This has done with the requirement of multiple documents and eliminated duplicate or fake beneficiaries. Over Rs. 52 lakh crore has been transferred through DBT nationwide. Unified Payments Interface (UPI): UPI serves more than 55.49 crore individuals, 6.5 crore merchants, and connects 731 banks on one platform, making it the world’s largest digital payment system. UPI powers 85% of India’s digital payments and nearly 50% of global real-time digital payments. DigiLocker: The platform has over 71.66 crore registered users, with more than 936.03 crore documents issued by 2,822 onboarded issuers. Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance (UMANG): The platform offers 2,575 services for individuals, including 48 services integrated by the Government of Madhya Pradesh. e-Sanjeevani facilitates quick and easy access to doctors and medical specialists directly from your smartphone. The platform has served over 48 crore patients across the country. MeriPehchaan/National Single Sign-On (NSSO) is a user authentication service wherein a single set of credentials can provide access to multiple online applications or services. Currently, 17,540 services of various Ministries/States have been integrated with NSSO. Assisted delivery of services through Common Service Centres (CSCs) The CSC Scheme, a strategic cornerstone of NeGP approved in September 2006, was restructured as CSC 2.0 in August 2015 under Digital India, with the objective of establishing at least one CSC in each of the approximately 2.5 lakh Gram Panchayats in the country. CSCs are delivering a wide range of Government-to-Citizen (G2C), Business-to-Citizen (B2C), financial, educational, healthcare, utility, agriculture and other digital services. Over 800 digital services are being delivered through the CSC network, benefiting crores of citizens every year. State-wise (including MP) and district-wise (including Satna) list of CSCs may be seen at www.csc.gov.in . Total functional CSCs are as follows: As of May, 2014 As of May, 2026 Number of CSCs 83,950 5,01,731 2,56,743 Gram Panchayats have been covered with CSCs. During the financial years 2025-26, a total of 4854.03 lakh transactions were carried out through the CSC network while during 2014-15, a total of 457.29 lakh transaction was carried out, reflecting the scale of citizen-centric services availed through CSC network State-wise transaction details are enclosed at Annexure-I while district-wise transaction details for Madhya Pradesh, including Satna district, are enclosed at Annexure-II. e-District Mission Mode Project (MMP): The e-District MMP has enabled electronic delivery of high-volume citizen-centric services such as certificates (income, caste, domicile, birth and death), pensions, revenue services and licences at the district level. Nearly 2,000 e-District/e-Government services across all 36 States/UTs have been integrated with DigiLocker and the e-District platform, enabling anytime, anywhere access to citizens. District e-Governance Societies (DeGS): DeGS are registered societies under the respective State Governments and District Administrations.  They function as the nodal institutional mechanism at the district level and sub district levels for implementation and monitoring of e-District, CSC and other e-Governance/Digital India initiatives, including rollout of district service delivery infrastructure, capacity building, and coordination among district-level departments and stakeholders. Assessment of digital initiatives: The Government has, from time to time, undertaken assessment and impact studies of e-Governance initiatives under the Digital India Programme through periodic monitoring, stakeholder consultations and independent third-party evaluations. In 2025, a survey-based study titled “Digital India Program: Citizen Feedback & Actionable Insights” was conducted to assess digital adoption and its evolving impact. The study found that 90% of respondents were aware of and had used digital services, particularly Aadhaar, UPI/BHIM, Digilocker, Ration Card services and other digital services. Further, 71% accessed Digital India services at least once a month, of whom 77% reported increased usage over time. Additionally, 88% of respondents expressed pride in India’s Digital Public Infrastructure, such as Aadhaar and UPI, and its growing global recognition. The third-party evaluation of the Electronic Governance scheme was conducted through India Institute of Public administration (IIPA), Delhi in November, 2025. The study has highlighted that the Digital India Programme has significantly transformed citizen service delivery by leveraging technology to improve access to information and integrate government services. It has enhanced transparency, reduced service delivery time, promoted paperless and faceless governance, expanded digital inclusion, and empowered citizens through improved social and economic outcomes. Further, the following assessment was also undertaken to evaluate the impact of Common Services Centres (CSCs): An independent impact assessment of the Common Services Centres (CSC) Scheme (CSC 1.0) was carried out by the Centre for Innovations in Public Systems (CIPS), Hyderabad. It emerged from the assessment study of CSC 1.0 that the CSC initiative holds substantial potential for viability, and long-term sustainability. The CSC scheme is indeed a powerful vehicle not only for the efficient and effective delivery of citizen services but also for promoting entrepreneurship among the rural population and spurring socio-economic developmental activity. A mid-term impact assessment of CSC 2.0 was carried out by the Indian School of Business (ISB), Hyderabad. The report analysed that CSCs reduced citizens' travel distance by 27.25 km, travel time by 40.43 minutes, waiting time by 69.45 minutes, travel cost by ₹52.12, and wage loss by ₹179.44 per transaction. End-Term Impact Assessment was conducted by the Academy of Management Studies (AMS). The assessment reported that 98% of beneficiaries were able to obtain the required services through CSCs, 93% perceived a positive impact on their lives and 95% expressed satisfaction with the services delivered through CSCs. The Government has undertaken various measures to further strengthen CSCs as last-mile digital service delivery centres, which include: Expansion of broadband connectivity through BharatNet to Gram Panchayats and rural institutions. As of June 2026, a total of 2.21 lakh Gram Panchayats (GPs) has been made service-ready under the BharatNet Project across the country Expansion of the portfolio of citizen-centric digital services through CSCs CSC e-Governance Service India Limited has developed and implemented an AI-based Segmentation Module in the SPECTA platform for data-driven monitoring and analysis of CSC operations. The module leverages Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML) and Large Language Models (LLMs) to rank Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs) based on service delivery and transaction patterns and to categorize CSC services into appropriate business segments Chief Secretaries/Chief Administrators of States/UTs have also been requested in respect of strengthening the participation of State/UT Governments and District e-Governance Societies (DeGS) in CSC project implementation, VLE selection along with integration of State/UT e-District services with the CSC portal to improve VLE sustainability and citizen-centric service delivery. Enhancing the Digital Seva Portal, integration of additional Central and State Government services with digital seva portal alongwith Capacity building and skill development of Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs) Improving service delivery mechanisms and working in close coordination with Central Ministries, State Governments. *** Annexure-I State/UT-wise status of transactions through CSC ecosystem (portal + non-portal) during Financial Year 2025-26 State/UT No. of Transactions (Vol in lakh) during FY 2025-26 Andhra Pradesh 167.3 Arunachal Pradesh 1.81 Assam 118.17 Bihar 510.82 Chhattisgarh 215.69 Goa 1.31 Gujarat 125.13 Haryana 146.17 Himachal Pradesh 81.43 Jharkhand 181.13 Karnataka 124.89 Kerala 47.31 Madhya Pradesh 223.24 Maharashtra 340.53 Manipur 3.12 Meghalaya 10.57 Mizoram 3.97 Nagaland 2.33 Odisha 245.82 Punjab 54.13 Rajasthan 413.32 Sikkim 0.66 Tamil Nadu 120.98 Telangana 37.62 Tripura 23.23 Uttar Pradesh 1177.55 Uttarakhand 71.95 West Bengal 341.11 State Total 4791.28 Andaman & Nicobar 1.39 Chandigarh 0.41 Dadra &NH D&D 0.78 Delhi 21.55 Jammu & Kashmir 35.76 Ladakh 0.1 Lakshadweep 0.07 Puducherry 2.69 UT Total 62.75 GRAND TOTAL 4854.03 Annexure-II District wise Transaction in FY 2025-26 in the state of Madhya Pradesh Sl. Assessment of digital initiatives: The Government has, from time to time, undertaken assessment and impact studies of e-Governance initiatives under the Digital India Programme through periodic monitoring, stakeholder consultations and independent third-party evaluations. In 2025, a survey-based study titled “Digital India Program: Citizen Feedback & Actionable Insights” was conducted to assess digital adoption and its evolving impact. The study found that 90% of respondents were aware of and had used digital services, particularly Aadhaar, UPI/BHIM, Digilocker, Ration Card services and other digital services. Further, 71% accessed Digital India services at least once a month, of whom 77% reported increased usage over time. Additionally, 88% of respondents expressed pride in India’s Digital Public Infrastructure, such as Aadhaar and UPI, and its growing global recognition. The third-party evaluation of the Electronic Governance scheme was conducted through India Institute of Public administration (IIPA), Delhi in November, 2025. The study has highlighted that the Digital India Programme has significantly transformed citizen service delivery by leveraging technology to improve access to information and integrate government services. It has enhanced transparency, reduced service delivery time, promoted paperless and faceless governance, expanded digital inclusion, and empowered citizens through improved social and economic outcomes. Further, the following assessment was also undertaken to evaluate the impact of Common Services Centres (CSCs): An independent impact assessment of the Common Services Centres (CSC) Scheme (CSC 1.0) was carried out by the Centre for Innovations in Public Systems (CIPS), Hyderabad. It emerged from the assessment study of CSC 1.0 that the CSC initiative holds substantial potential for viability, and long-term sustainability. The CSC scheme is indeed a powerful vehicle not only for the efficient and effective delivery of citizen services but also for promoting entrepreneurship among the rural population and spurring socio-economic developmental activity. A mid-term impact assessment of CSC 2.0 was carried out by the Indian School of Business (ISB), Hyderabad. The report analysed that CSCs reduced citizens' travel distance by 27.25 km, travel time by 40.43 minutes, waiting time by 69.45 minutes, travel cost by ₹52.12, and wage loss by ₹179.44 per transaction. End-Term Impact Assessment was conducted by the Academy of Management Studies (AMS). The assessment reported that 98% of beneficiaries were able to obtain the required services through CSCs, 93% perceived a positive impact on their lives and 95% expressed satisfaction with the services delivered through CSCs. The Government has undertaken various measures to further strengthen CSCs as last-mile digital service delivery centres, which include: Expansion of broadband connectivity through BharatNet to Gram Panchayats and rural institutions. As of June 2026, a total of 2.21 lakh Gram Panchayats (GPs) has been made service-ready under the BharatNet Project across the country Expansion of the portfolio of citizen-centric digital services through CSCs CSC e-Governance Service India Limited has developed and implemented an AI-based Segmentation Module in the SPECTA platform for data-driven monitoring and analysis of CSC operations. The module leverages Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML) and Large Language Models (LLMs) to rank Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs) based on service delivery and transaction patterns and to categorize CSC services into appropriate business segments Chief Secretaries/Chief Administrators of States/UTs have also been requested in respect of strengthening the participation of State/UT Governments and District e-Governance Societies (DeGS) in CSC project implementation, VLE selection along with integration of State/UT e-District services with the CSC portal to improve VLE sustainability and citizen-centric service delivery. Enhancing the Digital Seva Portal, integration of additional Central and State Government services with digital seva portal alongwith Capacity building and skill development of Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs) Improving service delivery mechanisms and working in close coordination with Central Ministries, State Governments. *** Annexure-I State/UT-wise status of transactions through CSC ecosystem (portal + non-portal) during Financial Year 2025-26 State/UT No. of Transactions (Vol in lakh) during FY 2025-26 Andhra Pradesh 167.3 Arunachal Pradesh 1.81 Assam 118.17 Bihar 510.82 Chhattisgarh 215.69 Goa 1.31 Gujarat 125.13 Haryana 146.17 Himachal Pradesh 81.43 Jharkhand 181.13 Karnataka 124.89 Kerala 47.31 Madhya Pradesh 223.24 Maharashtra 340.53 Manipur 3.12 Meghalaya 10.57 Mizoram 3.97 Nagaland 2.33 Odisha 245.82 Punjab 54.13 Rajasthan 413.32 Sikkim 0.66 Tamil Nadu 120.98 Telangana 37.62 Tripura 23.23 Uttar Pradesh 1177.55 Uttarakhand 71.95 West Bengal 341.11 State Total 4791.28 Andaman & Nicobar 1.39 Chandigarh 0.41 Dadra &NH D&D 0.78 Delhi 21.55 Jammu & Kashmir 35.76 Ladakh 0.1 Lakshadweep 0.07 Puducherry 2.69 UT Total 62.75 GRAND TOTAL 4854.03 Annexure-II District wise Transaction in FY 2025-26 in the state of Madhya Pradesh Sl. ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
title: Tiger numbers and Tiger Reserves saw remarkable increase under PM Narendra Modi’s visionary leadership in last 12 years: Shri Bhupender Yadav
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change Tiger numbers and Tiger Reserves saw remarkable increase under PM Narendra Modi’s visionary leadership in last 12 years: Shri Bhupender Yadav Union Environment Minister addresses Global Tiger Day event in New Delhi, encourages People to respect Nature Wildlife Conservation stories go beyond Bare Data; they assimilate Traditional Knowledge, Emotions, Passion and years of Experience: Shri Yadav NTCA Eco-tourism webpage launched on Global Tiger Day 2026; NTCA Awards honour exemplary contributions to Tiger Conservation and Protected Area Management प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 12:21PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today addressed the Global Tiger Day 2026 celebrations organised by the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) in New Delhi. The Minister called for a deeper societal connect with nature and a conservation-oriented lifestyle. The event was graced by the presence of Union MoS (EFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh, besides senior government officials, wildlife experts, frontline forest personnel, students and other stakeholders to celebrate India’s achievements in tiger conservation and reaffirm the collective commitment towards protecting tigers and their habitats. Emphasising that conservation is not merely about protecting wildlife but also about developing a respectful relationship with nature, Shri Yadav said, “Nature is not only a source of tourism or entertainment, it also needs to be respected and people must derive peace from it.” He encouraged people to draw inspiration from nature and lead a lifestyle dedicated to environmental conservation. Highlighting India’s conservation achievements, the Minister said that the number of tigers (3682) and tiger reserves (58) has seen a remarkable increase under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. He added that the number of elephant reserves, national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, protected areas, community reserves and wetlands has also increased during the last 12 years. While launching the NTCA Eco-tourism webpage, Shri Yadav congratulated NTCA for bringing information relating to all Tiger Reserves on an integrated platform. It provides direct links to authentic websites of all Tiger Reserves for safari and accommodation bookings, making information more accessible while promoting responsible and sustainable nature-based tourism. (Link: https://ntca.gov.in/eco-tourism/ ) Speaking about the importance of documenting conservation experience, the Minister said, “The stories of forests is not bare data but it includes traditional knowledge, emotions, passion towards Wildlife Conservation and years long experiences of wildlife officers, Conservationists etc.” He urged forest officers to write more about wildlife conservation and share their experiences in a manner that can contribute to practical and implementable policy solutions. Shri Yadav also stressed the need for capacity building of the forest officers and staff by incorporating global best practices. He highlighted the role of the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) in taking knowledge sharing to the world under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. Recognising the contribution of those working on the ground for tiger conservation, NTCA Awards were presented to wildlife officers and other contributors for exemplary work in tiger conservation and protected area management. The celebrations also provided a platform to acknowledge the contribution of frontline personnel whose efforts are central to wildlife conservation. The Minister also reviewed an exhibition showcasing the best entries from the painting, sketching, slogan-writing and mask-making competitions organised on the theme ‘Save Tiger’ for school children across Delhi-NCR.  Further, a nationwide tiger conservation awareness campaign was also organised through Eco-clubs under the Ministry's Environment Education Programme, with special focus on schools located near Tiger Reserves. Five publications were released during the celebrations, reflecting NTCA’s continued emphasis on science-based conservation, knowledge sharing and public awareness. These include the July 2026 edition of NTCA Outreach Journal – STRIPES; the Security Audit Report of 24 Tiger Reserves; a report on habitat suitability assessment for Sloth Bears across Tiger Landscapes in India; Tigers of the World, published by IBCA and GTF; and The Rehman Khera Tiger, by Shri Chandra Prakash Goyal and Shri Satya Prakash Yadav. The Global Tiger Day 2026 celebrations reaffirmed India’s enduring commitment to tiger conservation through recognition of excellence, scientific management, capacity building, responsible eco-tourism, knowledge sharing and greater public participation in safeguarding the country’s rich natural heritage. Background: Global Tiger Day 2026 A century ago, an estimated 1,00,000 wild tigers roamed across Asia. Today, they occupy less than 8% of their historic range, and three subspecies—the Bali, Javan, and Caspian tigers—have become extinct. The decline in tiger populations has been driven by poaching, illegal wildlife trade, habitat loss and fragmentation, human-wildlife conflict, and climate change. Recognising the urgent need for collective action, the leaders of the 13 Tiger Range Countries came together at the St. Petersburg Tiger Summit in 2010 and launched the Global Tiger Recovery Program (GTRP). The Summit also established Global Tiger Day, to be observed annually on 29th July, with the ambitious TX2 goal of doubling the global wild tiger population by 2022. Since then, Global Tiger Day has served as a global platform to raise awareness about tiger conservation, strengthen international cooperation, encourage public participation, and review progress in protecting tigers and their habitats. ***** VM/GS/SK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290935) आगंतुक पटल  : 690 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Bengali , Assamese , Gujarati , Tamil , Telugu , Kannada , Malayalam Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change Tiger numbers and Tiger Reserves saw remarkable increase under PM Narendra Modi’s visionary leadership in last 12 years: Shri Bhupender Yadav Union Environment Minister addresses Global Tiger Day event in New Delhi, encourages People to respect Nature Wildlife Conservation stories go beyond Bare Data; they assimilate Traditional Knowledge, Emotions, Passion and years of Experience: Shri Yadav NTCA Eco-tourism webpage launched on Global Tiger Day 2026; NTCA Awards honour exemplary contributions to Tiger Conservation and Protected Area Management प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
title: Government Reaffirms Commitment to Strengthening India's Livestock and Dairy Sectors Through Targeted Schemes and Infrastructure Development
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Government Reaffirms Commitment to Strengthening India's Livestock and Dairy Sectors Through Targeted Schemes and Infrastructure Development प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 5:06PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India has reiterated its commitment to accelerating the growth of the livestock and dairy sectors through targeted schemes, infrastructure development, disease control, genetic improvement, and value-chain strengthening, while emphasizing that Animal Husbandry is a State subject under Article 246(3) of the Constitution. Replying to questions in the Rajya Sabha, the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying stated that there is no proposal to enact a comprehensive National Livestock Development legislation or policy framework, as legislative responsibility for animal husbandry rests with the States. However, the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD) continues to complement the efforts of States and Union Territories through a range of flagship schemes and policy interventions. Significant Growth in Livestock Sector The Government highlighted the remarkable progress achieved in the livestock sector over the past decade: Milk production has increased by 70% , rising from 146.31 million tonnes in 2014-15 to 248 million tonnes in 2024-25 . Egg production has grown by 90% , increasing from 78.48 billion eggs in 2014-15 to 149.11 billion eggs in 2024-25 . These achievements have been supported through key programmes including: Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) National Livestock Mission (NLM) Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP) National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD) Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) Focus on Exports, Traceability and Investment To enhance the global competitiveness of India's livestock sector, the Government is promoting exports through coordinated efforts with the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) and the Export Inspection Council (EIC). DAHD is also engaging with partner countries through bilateral mechanisms such as Joint Working Groups and Technical Working Groups to expand market access for Indian dairy products. A major initiative in this direction is the Bharat Pashudhan database, developed jointly by DAHD and the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB). Based on a unique 12-digit animal identification system, the database enables livestock traceability and supports the export of value-added livestock products. Investment in modern livestock infrastructure is being encouraged through schemes such as AHIDF and National Livestock Mission, while the Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme is working towards creating disease-free zones to improve export opportunities. India Remains Self-Sufficient in Milk Production The Government informed the Rajya Sabha that, according to the NITI Aayog Working Group Report on Crop Husbandry, Agriculture Inputs, Demand & Supply (2024), India's projected milk demand for 2025-26 is 243 million tonnes, whereas the country's milk production during 2024-25 reached 247.87 million tonnes. This demonstrates that India remains self-sufficient in meeting domestic demand for milk and milk products. Strengthening Dairy Processing and Rural Livelihoods To strengthen milk production, processing, marketing and rural livelihoods, DAHD is implementing several initiatives nationwide: Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) for conservation of indigenous breeds, genetic upgradation and enhanced milk productivity. National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD) providing: 50% grant assistance for strengthening milk procurement, chilling and quality assurance infrastructure. 75% Central Grant assistance for establishing modern milk procurement, processing, value addition and cold-chain infrastructure in hilly areas and the North Eastern Region. 70% Central Grant assistance for quality assurance infrastructure in these regions. Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) providing 3% interest subvention to eligible beneficiaries for establishing modern dairy processing, value addition and cold-chain infrastructure in both cooperative and private sectors. The Government also shared state-wise information on cooperative milk procurement, processing capacity and dairy infrastructure, noting that while data for the cooperative sector is maintained by DAHD, information relating to the private dairy sector is not centrally maintained. Supporting Farmers and Rural Economy The Ministry emphasized that the livestock sector continues to play a crucial role in generating employment, improving farmers' incomes, ensuring nutritional security, promoting exports and driving rural economic growth. Through continued collaboration with State Governments and sustained investment in infrastructure, technology and animal health, the Government remains committed to unlocking the full potential of India's livestock and dairy sectors. *** SM/ (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291173) आगंतुक पटल  : 82 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Government Reaffirms Commitment to Strengthening India's Livestock and Dairy Sectors Through Targeted Schemes and Infrastructure Development प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF CENTRAL FISHERIES SCHEMES IN GOA
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying IMPLEMENTATION OF CENTRAL FISHERIES SCHEMES IN GOA प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 2:55PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Government of India (GoI) is implementing Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) from financial year 2020-21 and Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) from financial year 2018-19 aimed towards a holistic development of fisheries in all the States and Union Territories (UTs) including Goa. Till date fisheries projects amounting to Rs. 147.23 crore under PMMSY and Rs. 107.00 crore under FIDF has been approved for the state of Goa. The details of projects sanctioned, year-wise, central assistance released and expenditure incurred in Goa under PMMSY and FIDF are at Annexure I (A & B) . In addition, the DoF, GoI is also implementing Central Sector Sub-scheme, Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) and launched the National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP) to facilitate formalisation of the fisheries and aquaculture sector through creation of a work-based digital identity and database for stakeholders. It also serves as 'one-stop' solution for access to institutional credit, strengthening of fisheries co-operatives, incentivizing aquaculture insurance, performance-based incentives, fisheries' traceability systems and training and capacity building. Further, the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) facility has also been extended to fisheries and fish farmers to meet their working capital requirements. (b)     Under the central schemes, beneficiary selection is done by the respective State Governments/Union Territory Administrations. Government of Goa has informed that about 463 beneficiaries covering fishermen, fish farmers, fisheries cooperative societies and self-help groups have been benefited under PMMSY. The component-wise details of the number of beneficiaries benefited under PMMSY are placed at Annexure-II . Additionally, it was informed that 4339 beneficiaries are covered unders approved FIDF Projects in the States of Goa. Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying PMMSY AND RGM IN BIHAR STATEMENT  REGARDING ‘PMMSY AND RGM IN BIHAR’ प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 2:54PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying has been implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) with a total outlay of Rs. 20,750 crore, with effect from the financial year 2020-21 for holistic development of fisheries and aquaculture sector in all States/ Union Territories including Bihar. Under PMMSY, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India has accorded approval for various fisheries developmental activities to the tune of Rs. 579.72 Crore with central share of Rs. 193.13 Crore, to the Government of Bihar. Out of this, as reported by the Government of Bihar, during the last three years from 2023-24 to 2025-26 total funds of Rs. 107.30 crore has been sanctioned by the State Government to various districts and a sum of Rs.73.59 crore have been utilized. The major projects approved for Bihar includes Integrated Aqua-park, Wholesale fish market, Integrated Development of Reservoirs, Referral laboratories for quality testing and Disease diagnostic, Fish Broodbank, hatcheries, etc. Besides, on 15 th June,2026, National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB) Regional office has been inaugurated at Patna for providing targeted training programme, exposure to best practices and continuous technical support to fisheries, entrepreneurs and other stake holders. The district-wise details of funds sanctioned, utilized and number of fish farmers benefitted in Bihar during last three years under the PMMSY are furnished at Annexure-I. In order to supplement the efforts of the States and Union Territories, Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Government of India is implementing Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) since December 2014 for the development and conservation of indigenous breeds, genetic upgradation of bovine population and enhancement of milk production and productivity thereby making milk production more remunerative to farmers across all the dairy farmers in the country including Bihar. The major interventions undertaken in Bihar include implementation of the 64.87 lakh Artificial Insemination Programme performed benefiting 29.16 lakh farmers, use of sex-sorted semen technology in 10,122 Artificial Insemination benefiting 9,020 farmers, establishment of a state-of-the-art semen station at Purnea, establishment of two In-Vitro Fertilization (IVF) laboratories at Patna and Motihari, training and equipping of 5,433 Multi-Purpose Artificial Insemination Technicians in Rural India (MAITRI’s) for doorstep Artificial Insemination services, and sanction of two Heifer Rearing Centres at Munger and Dumraon with a capacity of 500 heifers each.  Under the RGM program, the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India has released a sum of Rs. 79.29 crore to Government of Bihar and the same has been utilized by the State. Further, under the RGM, fertility camps, milk yield competition, calf rallies, farmers training programme, seminars and workshop, conclaves etc. to create awareness among the farmers about importance of indigenous bovine breeds have been organized across the country including Bihar. The district-wise number of farmers benefitted till date under Nationwide Artificial Insemination Programme of RGM is at Annexure-II. DAHD is also implementing the National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD) and the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) to strengthen milk processing, marketing, and rural livelihoods cross the country including Bihar. In Bihar, under NPDD, a chilling capacity of 7 lakh litres per day has been created, 21 dairy plant laboratories have been strengthened, and 13,590 village-level quality testing equipment have been provided. To strengthen marketing infrastructure, 3,426 deep freezers and visi coolers have also been supplied. In the last two years, under White Revolution initiatives, 11,834 Dairy Cooperative Societies (DCS) have been established. Under AHIDF, dairy processing units with a total capacity of 7.55 lakh litres per day (LLPD) have been approved in both private and cooperative sectors. **** Annexure-I STATEMENT REGARDING PMMSY AND RGM IN BIHAR FOR ANSWER ON 29/07/2026: District-wise details of funds sanctioned, utilized and number of fish farmers benefitted in Bihar during last three years under the PMMSY. Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying SUPPORT TO FISHERMEN COMMUNITY IN KERALA प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 2:52PM by PIB Delhi ‘Fisheries’ is a State subject, and the Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI) has not undertaken any independent assessment of the socio-economic conditions and livelihood challenges faced by traditional fishermen in Kerala.  Fisheries within 12 nautical miles (NM) of territorial waters is governed by respective Marine Fishing Regulation Act (MFRA) of the coastal States, whereas, fishing beyond 12 NM is under jurisdiction of Government of India. Accordingly, State Governments have their own regulatory framework/guidelines in place for development and management of fisheries in their jurisdiction. The Government of Kerala has informed that it continuously monitors and assesses the socio-economic conditions and livelihood challenges of traditional fisherfolk through field-level agencies, beneficiary databases, stakeholder consultations and periodic reviews. In addition, the DoF, GoI through its schemes, policies and programs has been taking several initiatives towards holistic development of fisheries in all States and Union Territories including Kerala. Welfare of fishers and strengthening their livelihood have been the core of these initiatives. The DoF, GoI, is implementing a flagship scheme Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), since 2020-21. During last 5 years and current year the DoF, GoI has approved fisheries developmental projects amounting to Rs. 1413.91 crore in Kerala. The approved activities inter-alia included interventions towards livelihood and fishers welfare namely, livelihood support for traditional fishers during the fishing ban period (1,71,033 Nos),  support for boats and fishing nets (200 units), establishment of Integrated Modern Coastal Fishing Villages (9 Nos), establishment of Climate Resilient Coastal Fishing Villages (6 Nos), procurement of  deep-sea fishing vessels (20 units), bivalve cultivation (1140 units) as additional employment, fish transportation units (468 units), installation of artificial reefs (42 units) for fish stocks enhancement, establishment of Matsya Seva Kendras (10 Nos) and engagement of Sagar Mitras (222 Nos) for extension and advisory services. In addition Kisan Credit Cards (KCCs) have been also extended to fishers to meet their short term credit requirements. So far, 18,908 Nos of KCC cards have been sanctioned to fishers and fish farmers in Kerala. The DoF, GoI in consultation with State Governments/UTs takes up needful interventions to enhance the resilience and sustainability of the fisheries sector from time to time. The PMMSY implemented by the DoF, GoI inter-alia envisages interventions towards sustainable harvesting of resources, development of modern costal fishing villages, climate resilient villages towards climate resilience. Assistance is also provided towards procurement of potential fishing zone (PFZ) devices, livelihood support during fishing ban period, group accidental insurance coverage to active fishers, additional and alternate livelihood activities like mariculture including seaweed cultivation, bivalve cultivation, open sea cage culture, ornamental fisheries, fish markets & kiosks, cold chain facilities, live fish vending centres, need based training and skill development programmes etc. Many of these interventions have been already approved to Kerala as detailed above, enabling strengthening of livelihood, promoting climate resilience and sustainability. The Government of Kerala has further informed that they are implementing various measures through the Department of Fisheries and allied agencies, including livelihood support schemes, promotion of sustainable fishing practices, modernization of fisheries infrastructure, diversification of income-generating activities, resource conservation initiatives and programmes aimed at enhancing the climate resilience of fishing communities. This I nformation was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Rajya Sabha in response to a question asked. **** JP. ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
title: FISHERMEN INSURANCE CLAIMS IN ANDHRA PRADESH UNDER GAIS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying FISHERMEN INSURANCE CLAIMS IN ANDHRA PRADESH UNDER GAIS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 2:50PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. Government of India is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) with a total cost of Rs. 20750/- crore from the financial year 2020-21 to till date for development of fisheries in all States/Union Territories including Andhra Pradesh.  The scheme inter-alia provides social security measure to fishers, fish workers through group accidental insurance coverage to both marine and inland fishers and allied fish workers wherein the entire insurance premium amount is shared between the Centre  and State in the ratio of 60:40, 90:10 for the Himalayan & North Eastern States and in the case of the Union Territories, the entire premium amount is paid by the Centre. The insurance coverage provided under the PMMSY includes (i) Rs.5,00,000/- against death or permanent total disability, (ii) Rs.2,50,000/- for permanent partial disability and (iii) hospitalization expenses in the event of accident for a sum of Rs. 25,000/.  Andhra Pradesh did not participate in Group Accidental Insurance Scheme (GAIS) during last five years. During the current financial year 2026-26, Proposal for coverage of 2,84,888 fishers have been received. Besides, the claim filing and settlement process under GAIS is governed by the policy terms and conditions. To simplify the process, standardized claim formats and checklists have been prescribed, timelines have been communicated to all States/UT, and regular coordination meetings are conducted with State Fisheries Departments, the insurance intermediary, and the insurance companies to address deficiencies, expedite submission of claim documents, and ensure timely settlement of eligible claims. and (d):  The Government of Andhra Pradesh has participated  in the Group Accident Insurance Scheme (GAIS) for the first time during the current financial year 2026-27  (01.06.2026 to 31.05.2027)  to extend insurance coverage to 2,84,888 fishers and no claims have been made till date for settlement. The Scheme Guidelines mandates that claim intimation is required to be submitted within 120 days from the date of the accident, and the complete claim proposal, along with all requisite documents, must be submitted within 180 days. Regular review meetings and follow up on the review are  conducted to expedite the process in a timely manner. This I nformation was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Rajya Sabha in response to a question asked. **** JP (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291002) आगंतुक पटल  : 105 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Telugu Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying FISHERMEN INSURANCE CLAIMS IN ANDHRA PRADESH UNDER GAIS प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: Union Health Minister Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda calls upon MPs from West Bengal to lead Jan Andolan for TB Elimination
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Union Health Minister Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda calls upon MPs from West Bengal to lead Jan Andolan for TB Elimination Says India has recorded a 21% decline in TB incidence, nearly double the global pace, with a treatment coverage rate of 92% Urges Members of Parliament to strengthen community participation, early detection and district-level monitoring to achieve TB elimination by 2030 Highlights indigenous innovations, AI-enabled diagnostics and enhanced patient support as key drivers of India's TB elimination journey प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 8:20PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of Health & Family Welfare Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda today chaired a meeting titled "Parliamentarians Championing a TB Mukt Bharat" with Members of Parliament from West Bengal on the sidelines of the Monsoon Session of Parliament at the Extended Parliament House Annexe, New Delhi. He was joined by Union Minister of State for Education & Development of North Eastern Region, Dr. Sukanta Majumdar. The meeting brought together Members of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha from West Bengal across party lines to strengthen collective efforts towards achieving a TB Mukt Bharat through greater political leadership and community participation. The meeting was part of a series of sensitisation interactions chaired by the Union Health Minister with Members of Parliament from states across the country, including Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and others. Shri Nadda informed the Members that similar consultations have been held with MPs from other States as well, as part of the Government's whole-of-government approach to accelerate TB elimination. The meeting reviewed the progress made under the 100-Day TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan , implemented in two phases to accelerate India's efforts towards TB elimination. The first phase, launched on 7th December 2024, initially covered 347 high-priority districts before being expanded nationwide and concluded on 24th March 2025. The second phase, launched on 24th March 2026, focused on nearly 1.58 lakh high-risk villages and urban wards across the country. Addressing the gathering, Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda described the campaign as "a defining moment in the nation's fight against tuberculosis, built on innovation, compassion and unwavering political will." He reiterated that the principal objective of the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan is to achieve the Sustainable Development Goal of eliminating tuberculosis by 2030. Highlighting India's remarkable progress, Shri Nadda cited the WHO Global TB Report 2025 and stated that India has recorded a 21% decline in TB incidence between 2015 and 2024 , compared to the global average decline of 12% , making India's pace of decline nearly twice the global average. He further noted that India's treatment coverage rate has reached 92% , significantly higher than the global average of 78% , reflecting the country's leadership in global TB control efforts. The Union Health Minister emphasized that TB Mukt Bharat is not merely a health programme but a nationwide people's movement requiring active public participation. Stressing the importance of Jan Bhagidari , he said that the campaign can achieve its full potential only through collective ownership involving elected representatives, governments, civil society and communities. Calling upon Members of Parliament to lead this movement in their constituencies, Shri Nadda urged them to: Regularly review TB elimination efforts with District Collectors/District Magistrates and the Health Department. Intensify awareness generation and stigma reduction while promoting early detection through Ni-kshay Shivirs and screening of high-risk villages and vulnerable populations, including asymptomatic TB cases. Strengthen oversight of TB programme implementation and service delivery through visits to district and block-level health facilities. Encourage community participation by mobilising Ni-kshay Mitras and local organisations to provide nutritional, psychosocial and livelihood support to TB patients. Organise targeted Ayushman Arogya Shivirs to proactively screen high-risk and vulnerable populations. Highlighting India's transformative TB elimination journey, Shri Nadda underscored the importance of universal mandatory notification of TB cases diagnosed in the private sector, alongside the provision of free government-supplied medicines to reduce the financial burden on patients. The Union Health Minister described the proactive detection of asymptomatic TB cases as a revolutionary step in the country's TB elimination strategy. He highlighted the role of indigenous TruNat molecular diagnostic machines in detecting Multi-Drug Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR-TB) and noted that AI-enabled handheld X-ray machines have significantly improved access to early diagnosis in remote and underserved areas. He added that portable X-ray units supported through PM CARES are further expanding doorstep diagnostic services across the country. Shri Nadda also highlighted the Government's patient-centric initiatives, including enhancement of the monthly nutritional support under the Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana to ₹1,000 per patient , introduction of shorter and advanced treatment regimens, and the mobilisation of over 5 lakh Ni-kshay Mitras nationwide to provide sustained nutritional and social support to TB patients. In his concluding remarks, Shri Nadda commended the parliamentarians for their commitment and expressed confidence that West Bengal has the potential to emerge as a leader in TB elimination. He observed that while the 100-Day Campaign has concluded, the real measure of success will lie in sustained progress across every district. Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava highlighted that West Bengal’s continued expansion of screening, treatment and patient support would be crucial in translating national progress into community-level impact. Additional Secretary and Mission Director, National Health Mission, Smt. Aradhana Patnaik, highlighted the technological backbone of India's TB elimination programme. She noted that molecular testing capacity has expanded from a few hundred machines a decade ago to more than 9,000 today, complemented by nearly 3,000 AI-enabled handheld X-ray units developed through indigenous innovation to ensure timely diagnosis across the country. Presenting West Bengal's performance across key indicators, she highlighted the state's progress in TB notifications, treatment success, preventive therapy coverage and alignment with national elimination targets. During the 100-Day Campaign, West Bengal implemented focused strategies by taking Ayushman Arogya Shivirs to urban slums, tea gardens, mining sites and migrant settlements, thereby bringing screening and care closer to vulnerable populations. The Members of Parliament from West Bengal collectively reaffirmed their commitment to intensifying awareness campaigns, reducing stigma, organising Ni-kshay Shivirs for early detection among vulnerable populations, strengthening oversight of TB services at district and block levels, and mobilising communities under the Jan Andolan through greater participation of Ni-kshay Mitras and local organisations to provide nutritional, psychosocial and livelihood support to TB patients. **** SR HFW/ HFM Meets WB MPs /29July2026/2 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291403) आगंतुक पटल  : 28 Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Union Health Minister Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda calls upon MPs from West Bengal to lead Jan Andolan for TB Elimination Says India has recorded a 21% decline in TB incidence, nearly double the global pace, with a treatment coverage rate of 92% Urges Members of Parliament to strengthen community participation, early detection and district-level monitoring to achieve TB elimination by 2030 Highlights indigenous innovations, AI-enabled diagnostics and enhanced patient support as key drivers of India's TB elimination journey प्रविष्टि तिथि:
