ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: Union Health Minister Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda Reviews Preparedness for NEET UG Counselling 2026
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Union Health Minister Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda Reviews Preparedness for NEET UG Counselling 2026 Reviews readiness of the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) for a seamless, transparent and technology-enabled counselling process Student-friendly counselling reforms introduced; one-time physical reporting, online document verification and enhanced facilities for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities Ensure Every Proactive Measure is Taken to Address Candidates' Concerns: Union Health Minister प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda today reviewed the preparedness for the forthcoming NEET UG Counselling 2026 , reaffirming the Government's commitment to ensuring a transparent, merit-based, technology-enabled and student-friendly admission process for undergraduate medical courses across the country. The review assessed the preparedness for counselling of All India Quota (AIQ) and other seats under the purview of the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC), Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS). During the review, the Minister assessed the preparedness of the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC), Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) and other stakeholders involved in the counselling process. He reviewed the counselling schedule, IT infrastructure, cybersecurity preparedness, grievance redressal mechanisms, candidate facilitation measures and coordination with participating institutions. Shri Nadda emphasized that the counselling process must be conducted in a transparent, fair and merit-based manner while ensuring a seamless experience for students. He directed officials to maintain robust technical support, ensure prompt grievance redressal and facilitate the smooth functioning of the counselling portal throughout the admission process. He directed the officials to ensure that every proactive measure is taken to address candidates' concerns. The Minister was informed that NEET UG Counselling 2026 introduces several major technology-enabled and student-centric reforms aimed at enhancing transparency, improving accessibility and simplifying the admission process. One of the key reforms is the introduction of a one-time physical reporting framework , significantly reducing the need for repeated visits by candidates. Following seat allotment, candidates will be able to exercise their willingness online by selecting either the Freeze or Float option. Candidates opting for the Freeze option will physically report to their allotted institute within the prescribed schedule to complete admission formalities, including verification of original documents and payment of the admission fee. Candidates opting for the Float option for participating in subsequent rounds for upgradation will be able to complete admission formalities, including document verification, through the online mode within the stipulated timeline. During this period, they will not be required to physically report to the allotted institute, submit original documents or pay the admission fee. Their provisional admission will remain valid while participating in subsequent counselling rounds. The upgradation facility will remain available up to the third round of counselling. After completion of the third round, candidates holding allotted seats will report physically to their respective institutions for verification of original documents, payment of admission fees and completion of institutional formalities. The revised framework ensures one-time physical reporting, one-time verification of original documents and one-time payment of admission fees , thereby reducing unnecessary travel, simplifying admission procedures and providing greater convenience to students. Another important reform introduced this year is the online resignation facility . Candidates wishing to resign from their allotted seat, wherever permitted under the applicable counselling rules and timelines, will now be able to submit their resignation through the MCC Counselling Portal without the need to physically visit the allotted institute, unless otherwise specified in the Information Bulletin or notified separately by MCC. The review also highlighted several measures to strengthen transparency and operational efficiency, including pre-populated candidate data received from the National Testing Agency (NTA), online document verification, validation of the seat matrix by the National Medical Commission (NMC) and verification by participating institutes. Special emphasis has been placed on improving accessibility for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) . To facilitate greater accessibility, transparency and uniformity in assessment, the number of designated assessment centres has been expanded from 16 to 61 across the country. In accordance with the National Medical Commission Guidelines dated 27 July 2026 , the certificate issued by designated Medical Boards will now be known as the "Eligibility Certificate" , reflecting its purpose of determining a candidate's eligibility for admission to the MBBS course based on functional assessment. The revised guidelines establish a transparent, uniform, evidence-based and competency-oriented framework for assessment of PwBD candidates while ensuring equal opportunity, academic standards, professional competence and patient safety. The new guidelines also provide for an Appellate Disability Assessment Board , enabling eligible candidates to appeal against the assessment of the initial Disability Assessment Board in accordance with the provisions of the Information Bulletin. Another significant reform is the complete digitisation of the admission process under the NRI category. Registration for NRI candidates will now be conducted entirely through the online counselling portal in accordance with the prescribed eligibility criteria. Candidates will upload all required documents online, replacing the earlier practice of submission through email. The uploaded documents will be verified online by designated Document Verification Officers, ensuring a transparent, efficient and time-bound verification process. MCC though its public notice issued on 27 th May, 2026 has already informed that the candidates applying under the NRI category will be required to submit evidentiary proof and relevant legal documents during the counselling process, in accordance with the directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, establishing that the sponsor is the bona fide legal guardian of the candidate under the provisions of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890. Shri Nadda was also informed that cybersecurity preparedness has been comprehensively reviewed in coordination with the National Informatics Centre (NIC). Training programmes have been conducted for Disability Assessment Boards, college nodal officers and Document Verification Officers to ensure uniform implementation of the counselling process across the country. To strengthen candidate support, a 24×7 toll-free call centre (1800-102-7637) has been established. Bilingual information material, frequently asked questions and guidance videos are also being made available through various platforms to assist candidates throughout the counselling process. A dedicated email-based grievance redressal mechanism ( mcc2026[at]gov[dot]in ) has also been established for prompt resolution of candidate queries. The National Testing Agency declared the NEET (UG) 2026 results on 16 July 2026 . The counselling process for All India Quota seats in MBBS, BDS and B.Sc. (Hons.) Nursing is expected to commence shortly. Candidates have been advised to carefully read the Information Bulletin, counselling scheme and applicable rules before exercising options relating to seat acceptance, upgradation, resignation or disability assessment. They have also been advised to regularly visit the official MCC counselling portal and adhere to the notified counselling schedule throughout the admission process. Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastva, Additional Secretary, Medical Education Smt. Vinod Kotwal, Director General of Health Services, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare Dr. Loveneesh G Krishna, Director General, National Informatics Centre Shri Priyank Bharti and other senior officials participated in the review meeting. *** SR HFW/HFM Reviews Preparedness for NEET UG Counselling 2026/29July2026/1 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291318) आगंतुक पटल  : 269 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Gujarati Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Union Health Minister Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda Reviews Preparedness for NEET UG Counselling 2026 Reviews readiness of the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) for a seamless, transparent and technology-enabled counselling process Student-friendly counselling reforms introduced; one-time physical reporting, online document verification and enhanced facilities for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities Ensure Every Proactive Measure is Taken to Address Candidates' Concerns: Union Health Minister प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                        29 JUL 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda today reviewed the preparedness for the forthcoming NEET UG Counselling 2026 , reaffirming the Government's commitment to ensuring a transparent, merit-based, technology-enabled and student-friendly admission process for undergraduate medical courses across the country. The review assessed the preparedness for counselling of All India Quota (AIQ) and other seats under the purview of the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC), Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS). During the review, the Minister assessed the preparedness of the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC), Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) and other stakeholders involved in the counselling process. He reviewed the counselling schedule, IT infrastructure, cybersecurity preparedness, grievance redressal mechanisms, candidate facilitation measures and coordination with participating institutions. Shri Nadda emphasized that the counselling process must be conducted in a transparent, fair and merit-based manner while ensuring a seamless experience for students. He directed officials to maintain robust technical support, ensure prompt grievance redressal and facilitate the smooth functioning of the counselling portal throughout the admission process. He directed the officials to ensure that every proactive measure is taken to address candidates' concerns. The Minister was informed that NEET UG Counselling 2026 introduces several major technology-enabled and student-centric reforms aimed at enhancing transparency, improving accessibility and simplifying the admission process. One of the key reforms is the introduction of a one-time physical reporting framework , significantly reducing the need for repeated visits by candidates. Following seat allotment, candidates will be able to exercise their willingness online by selecting either the Freeze or Float option. Candidates opting for the Freeze option will physically report to their allotted institute within the prescribed schedule to complete admission formalities, including verification of original documents and payment of the admission fee. Candidates opting for the Float option for participating in subsequent rounds for upgradation will be able to complete admission formalities, including document verification, through the online mode within the stipulated timeline. During this period, they will not be required to physically report to the allotted institute, submit original documents or pay the admission fee. Their provisional admission will remain valid while participating in subsequent counselling rounds. The upgradation facility will remain available up to the third round of counselling. After completion of the third round, candidates holding allotted seats will report physically to their respective institutions for verification of original documents, payment of admission fees and completion of institutional formalities. The revised framework ensures one-time physical reporting, one-time verification of original documents and one-time payment of admission fees , thereby reducing unnecessary travel, simplifying admission procedures and providing greater convenience to students. Another important reform introduced this year is the online resignation facility . Candidates wishing to resign from their allotted seat, wherever permitted under the applicable counselling rules and timelines, will now be able to submit their resignation through the MCC Counselling Portal without the need to physically visit the allotted institute, unless otherwise specified in the Information Bulletin or notified separately by MCC. The review also highlighted several measures to strengthen transparency and operational efficiency, including pre-populated candidate data received from the National Testing Agency (NTA), online document verification, validation of the seat matrix by the National Medical Commission (NMC) and verification by participating institutes. Special emphasis has been placed on improving accessibility for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) . To facilitate greater accessibility, transparency and uniformity in assessment, the number of designated assessment centres has been expanded from 16 to 61 across the country. In accordance with the National Medical Commission Guidelines dated 27 July 2026 , the certificate issued by designated Medical Boards will now be known as the "Eligibility Certificate" , reflecting its purpose of determining a candidate's eligibility for admission to the MBBS course based on functional assessment. The revised guidelines establish a transparent, uniform, evidence-based and competency-oriented framework for assessment of PwBD candidates while ensuring equal opportunity, academic standards, professional competence and patient safety. The new guidelines also provide for an Appellate Disability Assessment Board , enabling eligible candidates to appeal against the assessment of the initial Disability Assessment Board in accordance with the provisions of the Information Bulletin. Another significant reform is the complete digitisation of the admission process under the NRI category. Registration for NRI candidates will now be conducted entirely through the online counselling portal in accordance with the prescribed eligibility criteria. Candidates will upload all required documents online, replacing the earlier practice of submission through email. The uploaded documents will be verified online by designated Document Verification Officers, ensuring a transparent, efficient and time-bound verification process. MCC though its public notice issued on 27 th May, 2026 has already informed that the candidates applying under the NRI category will be required to submit evidentiary proof and relevant legal documents during the counselling process, in accordance with the directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, establishing that the sponsor is the bona fide legal guardian of the candidate under the provisions of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890. Shri Nadda was also informed that cybersecurity preparedness has been comprehensively reviewed in coordination with the National Informatics Centre (NIC). Training programmes have been conducted for Disability Assessment Boards, college nodal officers and Document Verification Officers to ensure uniform implementation of the counselling process across the country. To strengthen candidate support, a 24×7 toll-free call centre (1800-102-7637) has been established. Bilingual information material, frequently asked questions and guidance videos are also being made available through various platforms to assist candidates throughout the counselling process. A dedicated email-based grievance redressal mechanism ( mcc2026[at]gov[dot]in ) has also been established for prompt resolution of candidate queries. The National Testing Agency declared the NEET (UG) 2026 results on 16 July 2026 . The counselling process for All India Quota seats in MBBS, BDS and B.Sc. (Hons.) Nursing is expected to commence shortly. Candidates have been advised to carefully read the Information Bulletin, counselling scheme and applicable rules before exercising options relating to seat acceptance, upgradation, resignation or disability assessment. They have also been advised to regularly visit the official MCC counselling portal and adhere to the notified counselling schedule throughout the admission process. Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastva, Additional Secretary, Medical Education Smt. Vinod Kotwal, Director General of Health Services, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare Dr. Loveneesh G Krishna, Director General, National Informatics Centre Shri Priyank Bharti and other senior officials participated in the review meeting. *** SR HFW/HFM Reviews Preparedness for NEET UG Counselling 2026/29July2026/1 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291318)

                29 JUL 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) successfully conducted a Pre-Bid conference at India Habitat Centre, New Delhi, Global Tender for Selection of Manufacturers for Setting Up 10 GWh Manufacturing Capacities for Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) for Grid Scale Stationary Storage Applications under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme. title: Ministry of Heavy Industries Extends Bid Submission Timeline for Global Tender under Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnet (REPM scheme)
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Heavy Industries Ministry of Heavy Industries Extends Bid Submission Timeline for Global Tender under Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnet (REPM scheme) प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 5:16PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI), Government of India, has extended timelines for global tender under the REPM scheme. The Bid Due Date has been extended from 29.07.2026 to 12.08.2026, while the opening of Technical Bids has been rescheduled from 30.07.2026 to 13.08.2026 to facilitate wider participation and provide additional time for stakeholders in the bidding process. The Addendum has been published on the Central Public Procurement (CPP) Portal for information of all stakeholders. ( https://eprocure.gov.in/eprocure/app ). The global tender was invited by the Ministry on 20th March 2026 for selection of manufacturers as beneficiaries under REPM scheme to establish integrated rare earth permanent magnet manufacturing facilities in India. On 26th November 2025, the Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi approved the Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnet with a financial outlay of Rs. 7,280 Crore. The Scheme, a first-of-its-kind initiative, aims to establish a total capacity of 6,000 Metric Tons Per Annum (MTPA) of integrated Rare Earth Permanent Magnet manufacturing facilities in India, thereby enhancing self-reliance and positioning India as a key player in the global REPM market. Rare Earth Permanent Magnets are among the most powerful magnets in the world and are widely used in electric vehicles, wind turbines, high-end electronics, aerospace and defence systems. By building a complete value chain from NdPr oxide to finished magnets in India, the Scheme is expected to significantly reduce import dependence in this sector. **** TPJ (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291188) आगंतुक पटल  : 111 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Heavy Industries Ministry of Heavy Industries Extends Bid Submission Timeline for Global Tender under Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnet (REPM scheme) प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: ENHANCING THE FORENSIC CAPABILITIES
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs ENHANCING THE FORENSIC CAPABILITIES प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 3:47PM by PIB Delhi The “Police” and “Public Order” are State subjects under the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India and the responsibilities to maintain law and order, protection of life and property of the citizens including investigation, prosecution of crime and criminals, and related forensic science facilities, are with the State concerned. However, the Government of India, Ministry of Home Affairs has taken significant steps to strengthen the forensic eco-system in the country through various schemes including Nirbhaya Fund having consolidated financial outlay of more than ₹4800 crore, which includes: (i) A State-of-the-art DNA Analysis and Research & Development facility has been set up at the Central Forensic Sciences Laboratory at Chandigarh. (ii) Machinery & equipment have been upgraded in the Central Forensic Sciences Laboratories, including in the new disciplines of Forensics in Narcotic Drugs & Psychotropic Substances, Digital Forensics, DNA Forensic analysis, Forensic Psychology. (iii) A National Cyber Forensic Laboratory at the Central Forensic Sciences Laboratory, Hyderabad has been set up to investigate important cases of digital fraud / cyber forensics. Apart from this, setting up of 06 additional National Cyber Forensic Laboratories have been approved under the umbrella scheme “Safety of Women”. (iv) In addition to the already established 07 (seven) Central Forensic Science Laboratories (CFSLs) in the country located in Chandigarh, Delhi, Kamrup (Assam), Kolkata (West Bengal), Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh), Pune (Maharashtra), and Hyderabad (Telangana), approval has been provided for setting up of 08 new CFSLs in the country in Jammu (UT of Jammu & Kashmir), Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and Kerala. (v) The National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU) has been set up under the Act of the Parliament in the year 2020 for providing quality and trained forensic manpower across all parts of the country. Apart from the initial campuses of the NFSU in Gandhinagar (Gujarat) and Delhi, approval has been given for setting up of 14 additional campuses of the NFSU in Goa, Agartala (Tripura), Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh), Dharwad (Karnataka), Guwahati (Assam), Nagpur (Maharashtra), Khordha (Odisha), Raipur (Chhattisgarh), Chengalpattu (Tamil Nadu), Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal, Bihar, and Uttar Pradesh. The NFSU has also set up training academies in Imphal (Manipur) and Pune (Maharashtra). (vi) Assistance has been provided to 30 States and Union Territories under the Nirbhaya funded scheme for Strengthening of DNA Analysis and/or Cyber Forensic Capacities in State Forensic Science Laboratories. vii) The Government is undertaking training for Investigating Officers, Prosecutors, and Medical Officers from States/UTs in collection, storage and handling of DNA evidence and use of Sexual Assault Evidence Collection Kits. The Bureau of Police Research and Development (BPR&D) and the LNJN National Institute of Criminology and Forensic Sciences (now Delhi campus of the National Forensic Sciences University) have trained so far 37,978 Investigating Officers, Prosecutors and Medical Officers. (viii) Under the Scheme for Modernization of Forensic Capacities, ₹420 crore have been approved for “Modernization / Upgradation of Forensic Science Laboratories in States / Union Territories” and ₹496.66 crore have been approved for providing “Mobile Forensic Vans for all districts and State FSLs in the country”. ix) The Government has approved establishment of National Forensic Data Centre under the umbrella scheme “Safety of Women” to systematically stockpile the forensic data received from all forensic labs for an efficient evidence management system. title: CROSS-BORDER NARCOTICS TRAFFICKING AND BORDER SECURITY
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs CROSS-BORDER NARCOTICS TRAFFICKING AND BORDER SECURITY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 3:45PM by PIB Delhi Cross-border drug trafficking continues to pose a significant challenge in the country, including the North-Eastern States. Due to their proximity to the Death Triangle and porous borders with Myanmar, the North Eastern States   remain   particularly   vulnerable   to   transnational   trafficking   of Amphetamine Type Stimulants (ATS) and Heroin through organised cross border trafficking networks. As reported by various Drug Law Enforcement Agencies (DLEAs) to Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), a total of 4626 kg of Amphetamine Type Stimulants (ATS) and 2652 kg of Heroin has been seized during 2021 to 2025. The vulnerable border stretches with Free Movement Regime (FMR) has facilitated drug trafficking activities in North-Eastern region.  Drug trafficking syndicates continue to adopt changing modus operandi, including concealment in legitimate trade and passenger movements, coordination through local receiver networks to facilitate illicit trafficking and change in trafficking routes to counter enforcement measures. To address these challenges, Government has taken various measures, some of which are as under: - (i)       To address the challenge of illicit drug trafficking & abuse of drugs, Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029) has been released on 26.06.2026. The Vision Document is to be implemented by the concerned Central Ministries/ Departments/ agencies and the State Governments/UTs as per the action points and timelines specifically mentioned for each Central Ministry/ Department/ Agency. The four key focus areas outlined in the vision document are as under: - Enforcement (Intelligence & Operations) Precursors & Synthetic Drugs Control Demand & Harm Reduction Capacity Building & Coordination (ii)      Established a 4-tier Narco-Coordination Centre (NCORD) mechanism for ensuring better coordination between Central & State Drug Law Enforcement Agencies and other stakeholders in the field of controlling drug trafficking and drug abuse in India. The Apex and Executive Committee of NCORD meetings are held in the Centre, whereas State-level NCORD meetings are chaired by the Chief Secretary on a quarterly basis and District-level NCORD meetings are held monthly under the chairmanship of the District Magistrate to review enforcement, intelligence sharing and preventive measures. (iii)     Joint Coordination Committee (JCC) meetings are held regularly in which all relevant Central and State agencies participate, to discuss investigation of important narcotics cases in the State. (iv)     A dedicated Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) headed by Additional Director General/ Inspector General level Police Officer is established in each State/UT to function as the NCORD Secretariat for the State/UT and follow-up on compliance of decisions taken in NCORD meetings at different levels. (v)      Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) has been regularly coordinating with other agencies like, Indian Navy, Indian Coast Guard, Border Security Force, State ANTF etc. to conduct joint operations to control the drug trafficking. (vi)     To enhance coordination with State Authorities, facilitate real-time intelligence sharing, for ensuring effective operational efficiency and to improve the geographical footprint of the bureau, NCB has established Zonal Units in key border areas such as Srinagar, Siliguri, Agartala and Itanagar and sub-zones have been upgraded to zones. Further, Government has approved the establishment of six new Zonal offices out of which four are being established in North-Eastern States i.e. Dimapur (Nagaland), Aizwal (Mizoram), Shillong (Meghlaya) and Gangtok (Sikkim). (vii)    Government is extending comprehensive support for combating trans-border narcotics trafficking through various means like deployment of advanced Anti-drone systems along most vulnerable stretches, installation of enhanced surveillance systems including CCTV cameras, PTZ, NVD, strengthening border fencing through installation of new design fence, Border flood light etc. The pattern of narcotics trafficking through the North-Eastern Region has undergone significant changes in terms of the type of drugs trafficked, trafficking routes and modus operandi adopted by drug trafficking syndicates.                         29 JUL 2026 3:45PM by PIB Delhi Cross-border drug trafficking continues to pose a significant challenge in the country, including the North-Eastern States. Due to their proximity to the Death Triangle and porous borders with Myanmar, the North Eastern States   remain   particularly   vulnerable   to   transnational   trafficking   of Amphetamine Type Stimulants (ATS) and Heroin through organised cross border trafficking networks. As reported by various Drug Law Enforcement Agencies (DLEAs) to Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), a total of 4626 kg of Amphetamine Type Stimulants (ATS) and 2652 kg of Heroin has been seized during 2021 to 2025. The vulnerable border stretches with Free Movement Regime (FMR) has facilitated drug trafficking activities in North-Eastern region.  Drug trafficking syndicates continue to adopt changing modus operandi, including concealment in legitimate trade and passenger movements, coordination through local receiver networks to facilitate illicit trafficking and change in trafficking routes to counter enforcement measures. To address these challenges, Government has taken various measures, some of which are as under: - (i)       To address the challenge of illicit drug trafficking & abuse of drugs, Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029) has been released on 26.06.2026. The Vision Document is to be implemented by the concerned Central Ministries/ Departments/ agencies and the State Governments/UTs as per the action points and timelines specifically mentioned for each Central Ministry/ Department/ Agency. The Apex and Executive Committee of NCORD meetings are held in the Centre, whereas State-level NCORD meetings are chaired by the Chief Secretary on a quarterly basis and District-level NCORD meetings are held monthly under the chairmanship of the District Magistrate to review enforcement, intelligence sharing and preventive measures. (iii)     Joint Coordination Committee (JCC) meetings are held regularly in which all relevant Central and State agencies participate, to discuss investigation of important narcotics cases in the State. (iv)     A dedicated Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) headed by Additional Director General/ Inspector General level Police Officer is established in each State/UT to function as the NCORD Secretariat for the State/UT and follow-up on compliance of decisions taken in NCORD meetings at different levels. (v)      Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) has been regularly coordinating with other agencies like, Indian Navy, Indian Coast Guard, Border Security Force, State ANTF etc. to conduct joint operations to control the drug trafficking. (vi)     To enhance coordination with State Authorities, facilitate real-time intelligence sharing, for ensuring effective operational efficiency and to improve the geographical footprint of the bureau, NCB has established Zonal Units in key border areas such as Srinagar, Siliguri, Agartala and Itanagar and sub-zones have been upgraded to zones. Further, Government has approved the establishment of six new Zonal offices out of which four are being established in North-Eastern States i.e. Dimapur (Nagaland), Aizwal (Mizoram), Shillong (Meghlaya) and Gangtok (Sikkim).                 29 JUL 2026 3:43PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Home Affairs administers Swatantrata Sainik Samman Yojana, a scheme for grant of pension to Freedom Fighters and their eligible dependents. Central Samman Pension under the scheme is granted only to those Freedom Fighters who fulfill the eligibility criteria and evidentiary requirements prescribed under the Scheme and apply for the same through the  concerned State  Government.  As on date, total number of beneficiaries under the scheme are 12,898 which includes 1,553 Freedom Fighters and 11,345 eligible dependents. The Swatantrata Sainik Samman Yojana is a Central Sector Scheme. The Third Party evaluation of the scheme is carried out at the time of continuation of the scheme from one Finance Commission cycle to another Finance Commission Cycle. Accordingly, the last third party evaluation of the scheme was carried out at the time of continuation of the scheme for 15 th Finance Commission Cycle through I ndian Institute of Public Administration (IIPA) in December, 2020. title: STATUS OF NAXALISM IN THE COUNTRY
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs STATUS OF NAXALISM IN THE COUNTRY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 3:41PM by PIB Delhi As per Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India, subjects of Police and Public Order are with the State Governments. However, the Government of India (GoI) has been supplementing the efforts of States that were affected by Left Wing Extremism (LWE). To address the LWE menace holistically, a “National Policy and Action Plan to address LWE” was approved in 2015 which focused on Whole of Government approach. It envisages a multi-pronged strategy involving security related measures, development interventions, ensuring rights and entitlements of local communities etc. After nearly six decades of violence, the country became free from Left Wing Extremism, which was once considered one of the biggest threats to the Internal security of this country. This has been achieved with resolute implementation of the “National Policy and Action Plan to address Left-Wing Extremism” 2015 and the coordinated efforts of Centre and State governments. At present, no district is categorized as LWE affected. The number of Naxal-affected districts reduced from 126 to 90 in April-2018, 70 in July-2021, 38 in April 2024, 08 in December, 2025 and to “zero” in March/April 2026. Presently, 37 districts are categorized as ‘Legacy & Thrust’ districts, which are no more LWE affected, but continued support in respect of security and development measures is required for some more time to consolidate the position. One (01) district has been kept under the category of 'District of Concern’, where LWE violent activities have been totally contained and their organizational structure has been completely dismantled. Although these districts are now free from LWE, security surveillance and developmental interventions are to be continued for some more time so as to preclude any possibility of their relapse. On security front, the GoI assists the erstwhile LWE affected States by providing Central Armed Police Forces and raising of India Reserve Battalions, helicopter support, strengthening of security camp infrastructure, training, funds for modernization of State police forces, equipment & arms, sharing of intelligence, construction of Fortified Police Stations etc. For capacity building of states since 2014-15, Rs. 3805.04 crore have been released to LWE affected states on operational expenditure and training needs of Security Forces, rehabilitation of surrendered LWE cadre, ex-gratia to families of martyred security force personnel/civilians killed in LWE violence etc. under Security Related Expenditure (SRE) scheme. GoI and State Governments have formulated comprehensive surrender-cum-rehabilitation policies.  The GoI also supports the States in the endeavor through ‘Surrender-cum-Rehabilitation’ Policy as part of Security Related Expenditure (SRE) Scheme.  The GoI reimburses the expenditure incurred by the LWE affected States on rehabilitation of surrenderees under the SRE Scheme.  The rehabilitation package inter-alia, includes an immediate grant of Rs. 5 lakhs for higher ranked LWE cadres and Rs 2.5 lakhs for other LWE cadres.  In addition, incentives for surrender of weapons/ammunition are also provided under the Scheme.  Provision also exists for imparting training in trade/vocation of their liking with monthly stipend of Rs. 10,000/- for three years. The efforts of the States for equipping and modernizing their police forces have been supplemented under the scheme of “Modernization of Police Forces”.  Under the Scheme, central assistance is provided to the State Governments for weapons, equipment for Information Technology, Communication, Training, construction of Police stations, mobility and construction of police housing and other police infrastructure etc. Under its sub scheme i.e. Special Infrastructure Scheme (SIS), works of Rs. 1761 crore have been sanctioned to LWE affected states for strengthening of State’s Special Forces, Special Intelligence Branches (SIBs), District Police and construction of Fortified Police Stations (FPS). The GoI’s focus on security infrastructure has been pivotal. So far 663 fortified police stations have been built. Under Assistance to Central Agencies for LWE Management (ACALWEMS) Scheme, assistance is provided for basic structure of camps and for provisioning of helicopters for counter LWE operations. Rs1303.68 Crores has been provided to Central Agencies through this scheme since 2014-15. There has been a special focus on the financial choking of LWEs and unearthing   of  the   nexus   between   CPI  (Maoists)   and  its  financial supporters. Coordinated actions by State Police in cooperation with Central agencies by various means have paid great dividends in choking the funds and resources supplied to the Left Wing Extremists in the past. On development front, apart from the flagship schemes of the Government of India (Gol), several LWE specific initiatives have been taken with special thrust on expansion of road network, improving telecommunication connectivity, education, skill development and financial inclusion in these areas. A few of these initiatives undertaken on development front are enumerated below: For expansion of road network, 15,189 km have been constructed under 02 LWE specific schemes namely Road Requirement Plan (RRP) and Road Connectivity Project for LWE Affected Areas (RCPLWEA).  In addition to this, GoI has also approved 127.08 km critical roads and 06 critical bridge to be constructed by Border Road Organisation in the erstwhile LWE affected area of Chhattisgarh state. For improving telecom connectivity in erstwhile LWE affected areas, 9,497 towers have been commissioned. For Skill Development, 47 Industrial Training Institutes (ITI) and 49 Skill Development Centres (SDC) have been opened. For quality education in tribal areas, 179 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) have been made functional. For financial inclusion, Department of Posts has opened 6,025 Post Offices with banking services in areas freed from Left-Wing Extremism. Also, 1804 Bank Branches and 1321 ATMs have been opened in these areas. Further, following the eradication of Left-Wing Extremism (LWE), one-third of the security camps in LWE-free areas are being converted into Jan Suvidha Kendras. These Kendras will provide a range of services, including livelihood promotion, skill development, access to government schemes, digital services, healthcare, and cultural and sports facilities to local communities. The first Jan Suvidha Kendra has been established at Netanar, Jagdalpur, Chhattisgarh, as the Shaheed Veer Gundadhur Seva Dera Kendra. For further impetus to development, funds are provided for filling critical gaps in public infrastructure in erstwhile LWE affected Districts under Special Central Assistance (SCA) scheme. Till now, approximately Rs. 4,289.20 crore have been released since the inception of Scheme in 2017 . For ensuring rights and entitlements of local communities, 21,26,268 title deeds have been distributed to beneficiaries (20,20,268 individual titles and 1,06,000 community titles). To further strengthen local self-governance in the erstwhile LWE affected areas, the Ministry of Home Affairs is carrying out a joint planning with the Ministry of Panchayati Raj. These measures reflect the Government’s commitment towards strengthening community rights and enhancing participatory governance in affected areas. The Ministry of Home Affairs has also conducted a survey in seven erstwhile Left Wing Extremism affected districts of Chhattisgarh to assess the extent of saturation of various government welfare schemes, developmental initiatives and the potential for livelihood generation through an independent agency. The survey has collated details of education levels, health indicators, and the availability of basic services such as primary schools, anganwadi centres, and secondary health facilities etc.  This is helping the Union Home Ministry and the State Government in fulfilling the objective of bridging the developmental gaps and ensuring livelihood. To engage youth and local communities in a constructive manner, the Government of India implements the Tribal Youth Exchange Programme (TYEP), under which tribal youth from erstwhile LWE-affected areas are taken on week-long exposure visits to different parts of the country. The Programme provides them an opportunity to interact with people from diverse regions and backgrounds, thereby promoting national integration, enhancing awareness of India’s rich cultural diversity, and providing exposure to the country’s industrial and developmental progress. Since 2014 total 37,655 tribal youths have participated in TYEP. Further, under the Civic Action Programme, GoI provides funds to CAPFs for undertaking various welfare-oriented activities in their operational areas, including medical camps, sports competitions and distribution of essential items among local communities. Under this Scheme, Rs. 221.88 crore has been released since 2014.  This has immensely helped in bridging the gap between the security forces and the local population. State wise details of the incidents of left-wing extremist violence, civilian deaths and Security Forces martyred during the last five years are at Annexure I.  Details of financial assistance released by the GoI to counter LWE under various schemes during the last five years are given at Annexure II.  Details of LWE affected districts in the last five years is given at    Annexure III. In the post-LWE scenario, the focus is on saturation of government welfare programmes, strengthening local self-governance, facilitating the rehabilitation of surrendered cadres, preservation of tribal identity and culture and expanding the reach of governance and public services in remote areas. Overall, GoI is committed for ensuring security and accelerated development of erstwhile LWE affected districts of the country. These Kendras will provide a range of services, including livelihood promotion, skill development, access to government schemes, digital services, healthcare, and cultural and sports facilities to local communities. The first Jan Suvidha Kendra has been established at Netanar, Jagdalpur, Chhattisgarh, as the Shaheed Veer Gundadhur Seva Dera Kendra. For further impetus to development, funds are provided for filling critical gaps in public infrastructure in erstwhile LWE affected Districts under Special Central Assistance (SCA) scheme. Till now, approximately Rs. 4,289.20 crore have been released since the inception of Scheme in 2017 . For ensuring rights and entitlements of local communities, 21,26,268 title deeds have been distributed to beneficiaries (20,20,268 individual titles and 1,06,000 community titles). To further strengthen local self-governance in the erstwhile LWE affected areas, the Ministry of Home Affairs is carrying out a joint planning with the Ministry of Panchayati Raj. These measures reflect the Government’s commitment towards strengthening community rights and enhancing participatory governance in affected areas. The Ministry of Home Affairs has also conducted a survey in seven erstwhile Left Wing Extremism affected districts of Chhattisgarh to assess the extent of saturation of various government welfare schemes, developmental initiatives and the potential for livelihood generation through an independent agency. The survey has collated details of education levels, health indicators, and the availability of basic services such as primary schools, anganwadi centres, and secondary health facilities etc.  This is helping the Union Home Ministry and the State Government in fulfilling the objective of bridging the developmental gaps and ensuring livelihood. To engage youth and local communities in a constructive manner, the Government of India implements the Tribal Youth Exchange Programme (TYEP), under which tribal youth from erstwhile LWE-affected areas are taken on week-long exposure visits to different parts of the country. The Programme provides them an opportunity to interact with people from diverse regions and backgrounds, thereby promoting national integration, enhancing awareness of India’s rich cultural diversity, and providing exposure to the country’s industrial and developmental progress. Since 2014 total 37,655 tribal youths have participated in TYEP. Further, under the Civic Action Programme, GoI provides funds to CAPFs for undertaking various welfare-oriented activities in their operational areas, including medical camps, sports competitions and distribution of essential items among local communities. Under this Scheme, Rs. 221.88 crore has been released since 2014.  This has immensely helped in bridging the gap between the security forces and the local population. State wise details of the incidents of left-wing extremist violence, civilian deaths and Security Forces martyred during the last five years are at Annexure I.  Details of financial assistance released by the GoI to counter LWE under various schemes during the last five years are given at Annexure II.  Details of LWE affected districts in the last five years is given at    Annexure III. In the post-LWE scenario, the focus is on saturation of government welfare programmes, strengthening local self-governance, facilitating the rehabilitation of surrendered cadres, preservation of tribal identity and culture and expanding the reach of governance and public services in remote areas. Overall, GoI is committed for ensuring security and accelerated development of erstwhile LWE affected districts of the country. title: INTEGRATED FLOOD EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT IN THE GANGA BASIN
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs INTEGRATED FLOOD EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT IN THE GANGA BASIN प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 3:40PM by PIB Delhi Central Government regularly reviews the effectiveness of disaster preparedness and emergency response mechanisms in flood- prone States including Bihar, in view of increasingly frequent extreme rainfall events. Based on the reviews, advisories and alerts are also issued to States/UTs for preventive measures. The issues of flood and river management are discussed between India and  Nepal  through  established  bilateral  mechanisms.  These  mechanisms include, inter alia, Joint Team on Flood Forecasting on rivers common to India and Nepal (JTFF), Joint Committee on Kosi and Gandak Projects (JCKGP), Joint Committee on Inundation and Flood Management (JCIFM) and Joint Committee on Water Resources (JCWR). Several steps have been taken to issue evacuation planning, resilient communication systems and emergency logistics in vulnerable districts, including flood emergency management framework for the ganga basin: (i) India Meteorological Department (IMD) and Central Water Commission (CWC) monitor various parameters based on Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Models to forecast rain and likely floods, including flash flood in different parts of the County for facilitating preventive actions by functionaries responsible for disaster management and taking preventive actions, alerting general public, etc. (ii)     Rain flood forecasting alerts are regularly generated by Central Water Commission (CWC), India Meteorological Department (IMD) and these are disseminated to the concerned States/Districts through State Emergency Operation Centres. (iii)    Communication of these alerts to general public and officials dealing with disaster management is also done through Sachet App, SMS based Common Alerting Protocol (CAP) and Cell Broadcast System. (iv)    Multi stakeholders and multi-State level Mock exercises are conducted by NDRF and NDMA to enhance preparedness. It has been stated by Bihar government that the state follows an integrated flood emergency management approach through coordinated action of the line departments such as Disaster Management Department, BSDMA, District Administrations, Water Resources Department, Home Department etc. The framework combines structural measures such as embankments, anti-erosion works and drainage improvement; with non-structural measures including flood forecasting, early warning systems, GIS- based monitoring, digital reporting, emergency response and inter-departmental coordination. This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha. ***** RK/RR/PR/PS/SC (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291040) आगंतुक पटल  : 84 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu Ministry of Home Affairs INTEGRATED FLOOD EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT IN THE GANGA BASIN प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: ACTION AGAINST DRUG TRAFFICKING
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs ACTION AGAINST DRUG TRAFFICKING प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 3:39PM by PIB Delhi The Drug Law Enforcement Agencies (DLEAs), are actively engaged in enforcement activity under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. These concerted efforts have resulted in significant achievements in term of drug seizures, registration of cases, arrests, disposal of seized drugs, destruction of illicit cultivation, financial investigations and preventive detention under Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (PITNDPS) Act, 1988, the details of which as reported by all DLEAs to Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) is at Annexure-I. Government has strengthened inter-ministerial and inter-agency coordination through restructured 4-tier (Apex, Executive, State & District level) Narco-Coordination (NCORD) mechanism by inclusion of various stakeholders at all four levels. It provides a structured, institutionalized platform for coordination among Central Ministries, State Governments and enforcement agencies for monitoring drug trafficking, precursor diversion, demand reduction and rehabilitation, resulting in improved enforcement outcomes and intelligence-sharing. NCORD has been consistently active and functional at the Apex, Executive, State and District levels. So far, 10 Apex NCORD meetings and 7 Executive NCORD meetings have been held to guide policy formulation, enhance inter-ministerial coordination and review the overall narcotics control framework. At the operational level, 272 State NCORD meetings and 16,187 District NCORD meetings have been conducted across the country, enabling coordinated enforcement action, intelligence sharing and regular monitoring of drug trafficking trends at the grassroots level. These meetings have strengthened cooperation among agencies, facilitated joint operations and supported focused interventions against drug trafficking networks operating across States. Also, an NCORD Portal has been created to act as a platform for all drug and NCB related information and also as a total Knowledge Management System (KMS) for all four tiers of the NCORD mechanism. It also acts as a repository of information on the anti-drug abuse initiatives of the Government of India. Over the last three years, the Government has significantly strengthened the Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) framework across the country. As on date, Anti-Narcotics Task Forces have been notified in all 36 States/Union Territories, though their mandate, structure and resources differ in various States/UTs. To address the issue, a template of an ideal State ANTF has been prepared and shared with the State/UT Governments by NCB in June, 2026. To improve the geographical footprint of the Narcotics Control Bureau, Zonal Offices have been increased from 13 to 30, across the Country by addition of 05 new Zonal Offices at Gorakhpur (Uttar Pradesh), Siliguri (West Bengal), Agartala (Tripura), Itanagar (Arunachal Pradesh) and Raipur (Chhattisgarh) and by upgradation of 12 existing Sub-zones as Zones. All 30 Zonal offices are operational with sanction of requisite man-power. Approval has also been accorded recently for establishment of Six (06) new Zonal Offices at Port Blair (Andaman & Nicobar Islands), Dimapur (Nagaland), Aizawl (Mizoram), Shimla (Himachal Pradesh), Shillong (Meghalaya) and Gangtok (Sikkim). The Government has implemented a centralized digital database, namely National Integrated Database on Arrested Narco-Offenders (NIDAAN), developed by the NCB in collaboration with the Inter-Operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS). The NIDAAN portal integrates data of Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) offenders arrested by all Drug Law Enforcement Agencies across the country, including information such as identity details, photographs, fingerprints, case particulars and court-related information. NIDAAN picks its data from all India E Prisons and the database of NCB. The database currently has around 9.50 lakh searchable data of arrested and convicted persons under NDPS Act. This database is accessible up to the Police Station level and to authorized users of State/ UT Police and Crime Law Enforcement Agencies (CLEAs). NIDAAN facilitates and assists investigating agencies in opposing bail, seeking cancellation of bail, monitoring habitual offenders, and supports preparation of proposals under the Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (PITNDPS) Act, 1988, thereby strengthening coordinated and proactive enforcement action. title: TECHNOLOGY-BASED JUSTICE SYSTEM
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs TECHNOLOGY-BASED JUSTICE SYSTEM प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 3:38PM by PIB Delhi The Government has taken following steps to significantly improve the speed, efficiency and transparency in Judicial Process :- Crime & Criminal Tracking Network and System ( CCTNS ) application aids computerization of police processes, from FIR registration to charge-sheet filing. CCTNS application enables investigation tracking, criminal records management, facilitate citizen services, and integration with Courts and other Pillars of Criminal Justice System. Timeline-based alerts as per provision of the Nyaya Sanhitas are configured in CCTNS application to ensure timely procedural compliance by the IOs. Interoperable Criminal Justice System (ICJS) Platform has been developed to facilitate police, courts, prisons, forensics, and prosecution to exchange data seamlessly. It facilitates electronic transmission of records including FIRs, charge-sheets, court orders, forensic reports, and prison data, reducing delays and enhancing transparency across justice delivery system. Investigation Tracking System for Sexual Offences ( ITSSO ) is a monitoring dashboard developed to track progress in investigation in cases related to women and children, especially sexual offences and timely submission of Charge-sheet as per the provision of Nyaya Sanhita . e-Sakshya mobile Application has been developed to create a secure, transparent and efficient digital ecosystem for capturing, managing primary digital evidence within the criminal justice system, enabling seamless coordination between Police, Prosecution, Courts and other stakeholders and ensuring integrity and authenticity of primary evidence from collection to presentation in court. e-Summons platform has been developed for streamlining the process of Generation, Transmission, Execution and Reporting of Court Processes in Electronic form. Medico Legal Examination and Postmortem Reporting ( MedLEaPR) Application has been developed as an end-to-end online solution for Medico Legal related cases. The application is used in Hospitals for the Medical Legal Examination and Postmortem Reports Generation. Nyay Shruti digital platform has been developed that facilitates virtual court appearances through video conferencing. It enables individuals such as the accused, witnesses, police officers, prosecutors and forensic experts to participate in judicial hearings remotely. e-Forensic Application has been developed as a digital platform which enables seamless and end-to-end case handling across all forensic laboratories. This platform helps enhance transparency, accuracy and efficiency, empowering Forensic Labs to securely manage evidence, automate workflows and deliver faster, data-driven forensic outcomes. e-Prison a cloud-based digital application has been developed to computerise and automate all prison and prisoner management operations across the country. It integrates jail databases into a single national network and facilitate sharing of prison data with Courts, Police and Forensic labs. e-Prosecution is a secure, workflow-based platform that enables structured digital coordination between the Police and Prosecution. It supports timely legal opinion and effective prosecutorial oversight before matters proceed to court. National Automated Fingerprint Identification System ( NAFIS ) is a centralized application that functions as a nationwide repository for Biometric Fingerprint data. It employs advanced algorithms to enable rapid, real-time matching of chance prints found at crime scenes against a national database of criminal records. It enables police, law enforcement agencies and fingerprint bureaux to securely capture, search and store the fingerprint records of accused, arrested and convicted individuals. This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha. ***** RK/RR/PR/PS/SC (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291038) आगंतुक पटल  : 117 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , Tamil Ministry of Home Affairs TECHNOLOGY-BASED JUSTICE SYSTEM प्रविष्टि तिथि:

Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs Shri Tokhan Sahu Visits HFA Division, Appreciates Team's Contribution Towards Realising the Vision of 'Housing for All' Over 127 Lakh Houses Sanctioned Under PMAY-U & PMAY-U 2.0; More Than 99 Lakh Completed and Over 96 Lakh Families Housed Nationwide प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 7:47PM by PIB Delhi Shri Tokhan Sahu, Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, reaffirming his commitment to engaging with the teams implementing the Ministry's flagship programmes, today paid a visit to the Housing for All (HFA) Division at Sankalp Bhawan, New Delhi. During the visit, Shri Sahu, accompanied by Shri Kuldip Narayan, Joint Secretary (HFA & Housing), and Shri R. K. Gautam, Deputy Director General (HFA), walked through different sections of the HFA Division and interacted with officials, consultants, young professionals and support staff at their workstations to gain first-hand insights into the Division's functioning. He held discussions with teams implementing PMAY-U 2.0, reviewing ongoing priorities, key initiatives and the progress of the Mission. He also listened to suggestions from the teams, appreciated their dedicated efforts in ensuring the timely and effective delivery of affordable housing to eligible urban beneficiaries, and acknowledged their invaluable contribution towards advancing one of the Government's most transformative urban missions. Shri Sahu also reviewed the PMAY-U Monitoring Dashboard, which provides a comprehensive overview of the Mission's progress through digital monitoring systems. Appreciating the use of technology and data-driven governance in improving transparency, accountability and real-time monitoring, he encouraged the team to continue adopting innovative approaches to make the implementation of the Mission more efficient and citizen-centric. Commending the dedicated efforts of the HFA Division, Shri Sahu noted that the Ministry has so far sanctioned over 127 lakh houses under PMAY-U & PMAY-U 2.0 , including more than 16 lakh houses under PMAY-U 2.0. Of these, over 121 lakh houses have been grounded, more than 99 lakh houses have been completed, and over 96 lakh families have already moved into their homes across the country. Addressing the HFA team, Shri Sahu said, "These remarkable achievements are a testament to the unwavering dedication, professionalism and commitment of every member of the HFA Division. Behind every completed house is a family whose life has been transformed. You are not merely building homes; you are creating opportunities, restoring dignity, providing security, and giving millions of citizens the foundation for a better future." Emphasising the inclusive nature of PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0, Shri Sahu highlighted that the Mission has empowered some of the most vulnerable sections of society. Of the total houses sanctioned, more than 21 lakh beneficiaries belong to the Scheduled Caste (SC) category, over 5 lakh to the Scheduled Tribe (ST) category, and nearly 50 lakh to the Other Backward Classes (OBC). Additionally, more than 22 lakh beneficiaries belong to minority communities, while over one crore houses have been sanctioned in the name of women or under joint ownership with male members of their families, reinforcing the Government's commitment to women's empowerment, social equity and financial security. Shri Sahu said that these achievements reflect the Government's steadfast commitment to ensuring that the benefits of development reach every section of society. He noted that PMAY-U 2.0 has emerged as a powerful instrument of social inclusion and empowerment, translating the vision of "Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas" into reality under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. Sharing his experiences from visits across various States and Union Territories, Shri Sahu recalled the heartfelt interactions he had with PMAY-U beneficiaries. He said that listening to the stories of families who had realised their dream of owning a pucca house reinforced the transformative impact of the Mission. "Whenever I visit different parts of the country, I meet beneficiaries whose lives have been transformed through PMAY-U. Their smiles and stories remind us that our work is touching millions of lives. I congratulate every officer, consultant and staff member of the HFA Division for their invaluable contribution towards this national mission and encourage them to continue working with the same dedication and commitment," Shri Sahu said. Concluding his visit Shri Sahu reiterated that PMAY-U 2.0 will continue to play a pivotal role in providing affordable housing to eligible urban families while strengthening the Government's commitment to inclusive urban development and the vision of a Viksit Bharat. **** SK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291365) आगंतुक पटल  : 25 Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs Shri Tokhan Sahu Visits HFA Division, Appreciates Team's Contribution Towards Realising the Vision of 'Housing for All' Over 127 Lakh Houses Sanctioned Under PMAY-U & PMAY-U 2.0; More Than 99 Lakh Completed and Over 96 Lakh Families Housed Nationwide प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: WAVES Digital Platforms Expand Business, Investment and Innovation Opportunities for the Media & Entertainment Sector
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Information & Broadcasting WAVES Digital Platforms Expand Business, Investment and Innovation Opportunities for the Media & Entertainment Sector IICT Stimulates Global Collaboration for Capacity Building and Innovation in India's AVGC-XR Ecosystem प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 3:56PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has established two digital platforms namely WAVES Bazaar and WaveX to strengthen the Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics and Extended Reality (AVGC-XR) ecosystem. WAVES Bazaar functions as a year-round global marketplace and engagement platform for the Media & Entertainment sector, facilitating structured business discovery, business-tobusiness meetings, market access, investment facilitation and international collaboration across films, animation, VFX, gaming, XR, immersive media, music and digital content. WaveX serves as a dedicated startup platform promoting innovation in the Media & Entertainment sector by facilitating access to funding through investor connect initiatives and a network of partners and incubators. While WaveX does not provide direct funding, it supports startups through incubation and pitching networking. The Government has established the Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT) as the National Centre of Excellence for AVGC-XR. IICT is in collaboration with the Government of Maharashtra and industry bodies. IICT has established international partnerships with leading global technology companies and academic institutions to strengthen the AVGC-XR ecosystem. These partnerships focus on curriculum co-development, specialized skill development programmes, access to advanced technologies, research and development, internships, startup incubation, scholarships, industry mentorship and international skill exchange. This information was provided by the Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan, in a written reply to an Unstarred Question in the Lok Sabha today. ***** Mahesh Kumar/ Vivek Vishwash/ Riya Rani (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291064) आगंतुक पटल  : 210 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Gujarati , Urdu , हिन्दी , Bengali , Assamese , Kannada , Malayalam Ministry of Information & Broadcasting WAVES Digital Platforms Expand Business, Investment and Innovation Opportunities for the Media & Entertainment Sector IICT Stimulates Global Collaboration for Capacity Building and Innovation in India's AVGC-XR Ecosystem प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Setting the Stage: India Targets Global Live Events Leadership by 2030
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Setting the Stage: India Targets Global Live Events Leadership by 2030 Model Licensing Framework, Heritage Venue SOP and Greenfield Venue Policy Among Major LEDC Reforms 29 States/UTs Designate Nodal Officers for Live Event Permissions on India Cine Hub Portal IIMC, in Collaboration with MESC and EEMA, to Develop Certificate and Short-Term Courses in Live Events प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 JUL 2026 3:16PM by PIB Delhi The Government has identified the live events sector as an important driver of economic growth, employment generation, tourism and cultural promotion. To facilitate the sustainable growth of the sector and position India as a global hub for live events by 2030, the Live Events Development Cell (LEDC) was constituted in July 2025. It is chaired by the Secretary (Ministry of Information and Broadcasting), with representatives of Central Ministries and Departments, State Governments, industry associations and other stakeholders. Four meetings of the LEDC have been held on 26.08.2025, 16.10.2025, 04.02.2026 and 30.04.2026, and has initiated several measures to strengthen infrastructure, simplify regulatory processes, promote ease of doing business and develop a robust ecosystem for the live events sector. The major outcomes are as under: An Execution Framework setting out a comprehensive strategy for the growth of the sector has been prepared and circulated to all stakeholders. An online system for live event permissions has been developed and made operational on the India Cine Hub (ICH) portal. It provides a single digital workflow covering application, coordination, approvals, payments and inspections, with timebound processing, real-time tracking, escalation of delays, integrated digital payments and digital audit trails. 29 States/UTs have designated their Nodal Officers for Live Event permissions on the ICH portal. The "Model Executive Order for Streamlining Licensing and Permissions for Live Events in India, 2026" has been prepared by LEDC and circulated to all States and Union Territories on 13.03.2026. At present, 3 States/Union Territory have implemented it in their State. The Archaeological Survey of India has framed a Standard Operating Procedure for organising live events at protected monuments and has shared a list of 224 heritage sites for the purpose. A concept note on a Greenfield Venue Development Policy has been prepared and circulated to State Governments, sports authorities and industry stakeholders. A Skilling Committee has been constituted. The Indian Institute of Mass Communication, in collaboration with the Media and Entertainment Skills Council and the Event and Entertainment Management Association, has undertaken preparatory work relating to certificate and short-term courses in live events and elective modules in its existing programmes. The LEDC has identified issues relating to visa and FRRO facilitation for visiting artists and crews, use of sports and heritage venues, streamlining of music licensing, permissions for events beyond 10 p.m., taxation and access to finance, and has shared these with the concerned Ministries and Departments for their consideration. Upon recommendation of LEDC, Reserve Bank of India has dispensed with the requirement of furnishing a Bank Guarantee for advance remittances of USD 500,000 and above for the import of services under the Foreign Exchange Management Regulations, 2026, notified on 15th January 2026. The regulations shall come into force from 01.10.2026. This information was provided by the Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan, in a written reply to an Unstarred Question in the Lok Sabha today. ***** Mahesh Kumar/ Vivek Vishwash (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291019) आगंतुक पटल  : 266 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Tamil , Urdu , हिन्दी , Bengali , Assamese , Gujarati , Telugu , Kannada , Malayalam Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Setting the Stage: India Targets Global Live Events Leadership by 2030 Model Licensing Framework, Heritage Venue SOP and Greenfield Venue Policy Among Major LEDC Reforms 29 States/UTs Designate Nodal Officers for Live Event Permissions on India Cine Hub Portal IIMC, in Collaboration with MESC and EEMA, to Develop Certificate and Short-Term Courses in Live Events प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: DAANVEER Initiative Launched; To Boost Digital Infrastructure Across India's Gram Panchayats
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Panchayati Raj DAANVEER Initiative Launched; To Boost Digital Infrastructure Across India's Gram Panchayats Citizens can Voluntarily Contribute  Computers to Gram Panchayats through Meri Panchayat App DAANVEER makes citizens active partners in building Digital India" : Shri Vivek Bharadwaj Posted On:
                29 JUL 2026 7:55PM by PIB Delhi DAANVEER, a citizen participation initiative to strengthen the digital infrastructure of Gram Panchayats across the country was launched today by Shri Vivek Bharadwaj, Secretary, Ministry of Panchayati Raj in New Delhi. DAANVEER is a platform designed  not just to close the immediate computer gap in the Gram Panchayats but to evolve into a long-term, citizen-powered ecosystem for strengthening local institutions. It is a transparent, end-to-end digital and verifiable platform that enables citizens and organisations to contribute towards the identified technology and infrastructure needs of Gram Panchayats in India. The initiative institutionalises the spirit of voluntarism in the society by providing a structured, accountable and seamless mechanism for supporting grassroots digital infrastructure. An initiative of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, it has been developed in collaboration with the National Informatics Centre (NIC) and DigiHaat. View this post on Instagram Launching the initiative , Shri Vivek Bharadwaj described DAANVEER as an important step towards realising the vision of Viksit Bharat by ensuring that every Gram Panchayat is digitally equipped, connected and future-ready. He said th at the initiative provides citizens across the globe, with an opportunity to reconnect with their roots by contributing meaningfully to the development of their native villages. Emphasising upon the transformative role of digital infrastructure at the grassroots, he observed that a computer in a Gram Panchayat is no longer merely a device for maintaining records; it is an enabler of faster service delivery, greater transparency and improved governance. He noted that DAANVEER should be viewed not as a donation drive, but as a platform for partnership that enables citizens and institutions to become active participants in strengthening local self-governance and advancing the vision of  Digital India. The State offici als participating in the event from Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra lauded the initiative and shared that several citizens and philanthropists in their respective States ha ve already shown keen interest in supporting Gram Panchayats by donating computers. They noted that strengthening digital infrastructure at the Panchayat level would significantly improve the efficiency, transparency and accessibility of public service delivery in the country. The launch was also attended by Smt. Mukta Shekhar, Joint Secretary MoPR; Smt. Palka Sahni, Joint Secretary MoPR; Shri Vipul Ujwal, Director MoPR along with senior officials from the State Panchayati Raj Departments from Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra. About DaanVeer DAANVEER builds upon India’s long tradition of voluntary public contribution while introducing a technology-enabled institutional framework to enhance trust, transparency and ease of participation. Drawing on the experience of earlier voluntary contribution models, the initiative incorporates verified institutional needs, standardised contribution options, end-to-end digital tracking, and direct delivery, thereby creating a credible standardized mechanism through which citizens can participate in strengthening public institutions. Carrying the tagline “Give Back to Your Village”, DAANVEER  is entirely voluntary. Available through the Meri Panchayat mobile application, DAANVEER enables individuals and organisations to contribute standardized, quality-verified computer bundles directly to eligible Gram Panchayats. The initiative integrates the Meri Panchayat app with the DigiHaat marketplace, allowing donors to choose from pre-approved computer bundles that are mapped to State-specific technical specifications. Delivery details are automatically populated, eliminating additional paperwork. Donors can also track their contribution from dispatch to installation and receive a digital certificate of appreciation in recognition of their support. Details of the initiative, including the list of eligible Gram Panchayats and the contribution process, are available through the Meri Panchayat app. India has nearly 2.5 lakh Gram Panchayats, which form the foundation of grassroots democracy and local service delivery. Building on the Ministry’s digital governance ecosystem-including e-GramSwaraj, Meri Panchayat, Sabha Saar, AuditOnline, Gram Manchitra and other digital platforms – DAANVEER seeks to bridge digital infrastructure gaps and ensure that every Gram Panchayat is equipped to deliver citizen-centric services efficiently and transparently. The initiative also provides citizens living away from their native villages, including members of the Indian diaspora, with a credible and transparent mechanism to contribute to the development of the Gram Panchayats to which they remain connected. Through DAANVEER, citizens can meaningfully participate in strengthening rural digital infrastructure while contributing to the broader vision of a digitally empowered and self-reliant rural India. *** AA (Release ID: 2291370) Visitor Counter : 119 Ministry of Panchayati Raj DAANVEER Initiative Launched; To Boost Digital Infrastructure Across India's Gram Panchayats Citizens can Voluntarily Contribute  Computers to Gram Panchayats through Meri Panchayat App DAANVEER makes citizens active partners in building Digital India" : Shri Vivek Bharadwaj Posted On:
